knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise Lipschitz underestimator formed from every simplex vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\} and let f:S\to\mathbb R be L-Lipschitz. Define q_S(x)=\max_{0\le i\le n}\{f(v_i)-L\|x-v_i\|_2\} and \widehat L_S=\min_{x\in S}q_S(x). Then q_S(x)\le f(x) for every x\in S, so \widehat L_S\le\min_S f. Moreover, \widehat L_S\ge\min_i f(v_i)-L\operatorname{diam}(S), so the all-vertex cone bound dominates the seed's crude diameter bound and has error at most L\operatorname{diam}(S).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of all vertex-centered downward Lipschitz cones is a valid pointwise underestimator and yields a bound at least as strong as the crude vertex-diameter bound.
assumptions_latex: f is L-Lipschitz on S in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_i f(v_i)-L\operatorname{diam}(S)\le\widehat L_S\le\min_{x\in S}f(x).

notation.meaning: Maximum of the vertex-centered downward Lipschitz cones.
Lower bound obtained by globally minimizing q_S over S.

knowledge_statements.title: Conical Subdivision Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary ray subdivision of a pointed simplicial search cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{r_1,\ldots,r_n\}\) be a pointed simplicial cone with linearly independent generators. Select two generators \(r_p,r_q\), set \(s=r_p+r_q\), and form \[K_p=\operatorname{cone}((R\setminus\{r_q\})\cup\{s\}),\qquad K_q=\operatorname{cone}((R\setminus\{r_p\})\cup\{s\}),\] where \(R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_n\}\). Replace \(K\) by these children, compute a valid lower bound on each child intersected with the prescribed radial domain, and prune children whose bounds fail the incumbent test. Stop when every active directional cell has angular diameter at most \(\delta\), returning the best feasible incumbent and the surviving cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplicial cone can be split by inserting a sum ray, after which child bounds guide pruning and angular refinement.
assumptions_latex: The searched radial domain is prescribed and bounded where required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=K_p\cup K_q\), the child interiors are disjoint, and certified child bounds permit safe pruning.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit geometry of nested simplicial cones under the stated bisection and concavity-cut subdivision rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\). Let \(K_h\) be nested cones vertexed at \(0\), each having exactly \(n\) edges. Suppose each \(K_{h+1}\) is a child of \(K_h\) in a subdivision by a ray meeting the concavity-cut hyperplane \(L_h\) at \(q^h\), and let the set \(\Delta\) of bisection indices be infinite. If \(\mathbb N\setminus\Delta\) is finite, then \(K_\infty=\bigcap_{h=1}^{\infty}K_h\) is the ray through \(q=\lim_{h\to\infty}q^h\in\partial C\). Otherwise, at least one cluster point of \(\{q^h:h\notin\Delta\}\) belongs to \(\partial C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If only finitely many subdivisions are not bisections, the nested cones limit to a ray whose limiting cut point is on the boundary of C. If non-bisection subdivisions occur infinitely often, their cut points have a boundary cluster point.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is compact and convex},\quad0\in\operatorname{int}C.
K_{h+1}\subseteq K_h\text{ are cones vertexed at }0\text{ with exactly }n\text{ edges}.
K_{h+1}\text{ is a child of }K_h\text{ generated by a ray meeting }L_h\text{ at }q^h.
\Delta=\{h:\text{the subdivision of }K_h\text{ is a bisection}\}\text{ is infinite}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\mathbb N\setminus\Delta|<\infty\Rightarrow K_\infty=\operatorname{ray}(q),\ q=\lim_hq^h\in\partial C;\quad |\mathbb N\setminus\Delta|=\infty\Rightarrow\operatorname{cluster}(\{q^h:h\notin\Delta\})\cap\partial C\ne\varnothing.

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoidal Partition Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic branch-and-bound using ellipsoidal node regions and certified lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial ellipsoid \(E_0=\{x:(x-c_0)^{\mathsf T}Q_0^{-1}(x-c_0)\leq 1\}\), initialize the active set as \(\mathcal A=\{E_0\}\) and an incumbent value \(U\). Select \(E\in\mathcal A\), construct finitely many ellipsoids \(E_1,\ldots,E_m\) satisfying \(X\cap E\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^m E_j\), and compute certified lower bounds \(L(E_j)\leq\inf\{f(x):x\in X\cap E_j\}\). Delete children with \(L(E_j)\geq U-\varepsilon\), update \(U\) using newly found feasible points, and insert the remaining children. Stop when \(\mathcal A=\varnothing\) or \(U-\min_{E\in\mathcal A}L(E)\leq\varepsilon\); output the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cover each selected ellipsoid by smaller ellipsoids, bound every child, discard noncompetitive children, and stop when the certified global gap is within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every node lower bound and every reported feasible objective value is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination by the gap test, the returned feasible incumbent \(\hat x\) satisfies \(f(\hat x)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\), where \(f^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Ellipsoid with center c and positive-definite shape matrix Q.
Certified lower bound for the node restricted to E.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonrectangular Bounding Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid lower bounding over general compact node regions rather than axis-aligned boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node region \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(F_R=X\cap R\) be its feasible portion. Any relaxation with feasible set \(\widehat F_R\supseteq F_R\) and objective underestimator \(\ell_R(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_R\) yields the valid bound \[L(R):=\inf_{x\in\widehat F_R}\ell_R(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x).\] The argument is independent of whether \(R\) is ellipsoidal, conical, simplicial, or another nonrectangular set. If \(R_1\subseteq R_2\) and the same exact restricted objective is used, then \(\inf_{F_{R_1}}f\geq\inf_{F_{R_2}}f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation remains a valid node bound on any region shape when it contains the node-feasible set and underestimates the objective there.
assumptions_latex: The displayed infima use the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(R)\) is a certified lower bound for minimizing \(f\) over \(X\cap R\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set restricted to node region R.
Relaxed feasible set used for bounding.

Variable-Domain Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe coordinate-domain reduction within a deterministic global-search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a box \(B=D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\), constraints defining \(F\), and optionally a cutoff \(f(x)\leq U\), initialize \(D_i^{(0)}=D_i\). At iteration \(k\), apply a sound contractor to obtain \(D_i^{(k+1)}\subseteq D_i^{(k)}\) such that \[F\cap B^{(k)}\subseteq B^{(k+1)}:=\prod_{i=1}^nD_i^{(k+1)}.\] Repeat until no domain changes beyond a prescribed tolerance or some domain becomes empty. Return the contracted box; if \(D_i^{(k+1)}=\varnothing\) for some \(i\), return a certified empty-node declaration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly shrink variable intervals while preserving every feasible point; an empty resulting interval certifies that the node is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is an initial interval box.
Every contractor application is inclusion-preserving for the node-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(B'\subseteq B\) satisfies \(F\cap B\subseteq B'\); hence removed points cannot contain a feasible solution.

notation.meaning: Feasible set, including any valid incumbent cutoff.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inclusion-preserving contraction algorithm is coherent and fits the leaf, but the broad deterministic-global-optimization locator does not inspectably support the contractor iteration and empty-domain certificate.

children.title: Constraint Propagation
children.top_down_role: Constraint-mediated transmission of domain reductions through a subproblem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits fixed-point and finite-termination claims for constraint propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Stopping before every contractor affected by a reduction is reconsidered may return a sound outer box but does not certify a common fixed point. On an infinite domain, exact propagation can also generate an infinite strictly descending chain unless a tolerance, finite representation, or other termination condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial propagation remains safe but may miss deductions, and exact propagation need not terminate on an infinite domain.
assumptions_latex: Every contractor actually applied is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{partial sound propagation}\not\Rightarrow\text{common fixed point or finite termination}.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature, Unfair, or Nonterminating Propagation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set preservation under finite compositions of sound constraint contractors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S=B^{(0)}\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^mF_j and suppose F_j\cap B\subseteq C_j(B)\subseteq B. For any finite contractor sequence, B^{(r)}=C_{j_r}(B^{(r-1)}) satisfies S\subseteq B^{(r)}\subseteq B^{(r-1)}. Thus B^{(r)}=\varnothing implies S=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any sequence of sound constraint contractors shrinks the box while retaining every jointly feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Every applied contractor is contractive and preserves the points satisfying its associated constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\subseteq B^{(r)}\subseteq B^{(0)},\qquad B^{(r)}=\varnothing\Longrightarrow S=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Jointly feasible portion of the initial box.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation Soundness Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination and greatest common fixed point for fair propagation on finitely many representable boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the representable boxes below B^{(0)} form a finite poset under inclusion. If every C_j is monotone and contractive and the schedule is fair, repeated propagation terminates at B^* with C_j(B^*)=B^* for every j. Moreover, B^* is the greatest common fixed point contained in B^{(0)}; hence it is independent of the fair schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair iteration of monotone contracting operators on a finite box lattice terminates at the schedule-independent greatest common fixed point below the initial box.
assumptions_latex: The representable box domain below B^{(0)} is finite.
Every C_j is monotone and contractive.
Every contractor is scheduled fairly until common stability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k<\infty:\ B^{(k)}=B^*,\quad \forall j\ C_j(B^*)=B^*.

notation.meaning: Greatest common propagation fixed point below the initial box.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Lattice Fair-Propagation Closure
Constraint Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point propagation of sound constraint contractors across shared variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a box \(B^{(0)}\) and constraints \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\), associate with each constraint a sound contractor \(C_j\) satisfying \(F_j\cap B\subseteq C_j(B)\subseteq B\), where \(F_j\) is the set satisfying \(c_j\). Initialize a queue with all contractors. Remove \(C_j\), set \(B^{(k+1)}=C_j(B^{(k)})\), and requeue contractors sharing any reduced variable. Stop when the queue is empty, a numerical contraction tolerance is met, or a coordinate domain is empty. Return the final box, or infeasibility in the empty-domain case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply sound constraint contractors repeatedly, revisiting affected constraints until a fixed point or empty domain is reached.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_j\) is contractive and preserves all points satisfying its associated constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the returned box \(B'\), \(B'\subseteq B^{(0)}\) and \(B^{(0)}\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^mF_j\subseteq B'\).

notation.meaning: Sound contractor associated with constraint j.
Set of points satisfying constraint j.
Variable box after k contractor applications.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The queue-based fixed-point propagation statement is mathematically sound, but its contractor scheduling and requeue rules require a constraint-propagation-specific source.

children.title: Expression-Range Tightening
children.top_down_role: Range refinement for intermediate expressions represented in a computational graph.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-consistency stopping condition for expression-range tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Intervals (Z_v)_v are propagation-stable when every forward intersection and every sound backward projection leaves them unchanged. This is a local-consistency condition and does not imply that every retained value participates in one common feasible graph evaluation or that the intervals are exact ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward-backward fixed point is locally stable but need not equal the exact joint range.
assumptions_latex: The primitive forward and backward operators are sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{propagation stability}\not\Rightarrow\text{global range exactness}.

notation.meaning: Stable interval at expression node v.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Graph Propagation Stability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of shared-variable dependence under occurrence-wise interval evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For h(x)=x-x on x\in[0,1], ordinary occurrence-wise interval evaluation gives [0,1]-[0,1]=[-1,1], although the exact range is \{0\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact range of x minus x is zero, while ordinary interval evaluation returns minus one to one.
assumptions_latex: The two occurrences are evaluated without an additional dependency representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{range}(x-x)=\{0\}\subsetneq[-1,1].

notation.meaning: Shared variable and its interval domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-Limited Tightening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion invariant for forward-backward expression-graph tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every primitive forward image and backward inverse-image operator is inclusion-preserving, each sweep produces Z'_v\subseteq Z_v at every graph node while retaining the value induced by every input satisfying the root requirement. An empty node interval therefore proves that no admissible input exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound forward-backward tightening shrinks expression intervals without removing any admissible graph evaluation.
assumptions_latex: Every primitive forward and backward interval operator is inclusion-preserving.
All intersections and rounding operations are validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z'_v\subseteq Z_v\text{ and every admissible evaluation remains in }Z'_v.

notation.meaning: Interval attached to expression node v.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression-Range Contraction Invariant
Expression-Range Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward interval tightening on an expression graph inside one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an expression graph for \(y=h(x)\), a variable box \(B\), and an admissible output interval \(Y\), initialize each variable node with its interval from \(B\). Perform a forward interval evaluation to enclose every intermediate expression and obtain \(H(B)\supseteq h(B)\). Replace the root interval by \(H(B)\cap Y\), then propagate inverse interval images backward through each operation, intersecting every child interval with its inferred range. Iterate forward and backward sweeps until no material change or an interval becomes empty; output the tightened variable box or certified emptiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate expression ranges forward, intersect with required outputs, and propagate inverse ranges backward to tighten variables without losing feasible points.
assumptions_latex: Every forward extension encloses the exact range of its operation.
Every backward operation returns an inclusion-preserving inverse enclosure.
All interval intersections use outward-rounded arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output box \(B'\subseteq B\) contains every \(x\in B\) satisfying \(h(x)\in Y\); an empty interval certifies that no such \(x\) exists.

notation.meaning: Interval enclosure of the range h(B).
Admissible interval for the expression output.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward-backward interval algorithm and enclosure conclusion fit the leaf, but no citation supports the outward-rounded inverse-propagation guarantees.

children.title: Search-Tree Primal-Bound Management
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for search-tree prioritization and primal-bound management.

children.title: Node Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies for prioritizing open subproblems in the search tree.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Selection Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rules for choosing the next active subproblem in spatial branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A_k\) be the finite active-node set at iteration \(k\), with certified lower bounds \(L(N)\), depths \(d(N)\), and insertion times \(t(N)\). A node-selection policy returns one node \(N_k\in\mathcal A_k\). Best-bound selection chooses \(N_k\in\arg\min_{N\in\mathcal A_k}L(N)\); depth-first selection chooses a node of maximal depth, breaking ties by recency; breadth-first selection chooses one of minimal depth, breaking ties by age. After processing \(N_k\), remove it, insert its unfathomed children, and repeat until the active set is empty or the global stopping test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an active node by best bound, depth, or age, process it, insert surviving children, and repeat until certified termination.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A_k\) is finite and nonempty whenever selection is requested.
Tie-breaking is deterministic or otherwise guaranteed to return an active node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration selects exactly one member of \(\mathcal A_k\); best-bound selection attains \(\min_{N\in\mathcal A_k}L(N)\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound of node N.
Depth of node N in the search tree.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-starvation condition used by infinite-search convergence arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node-selection policy is fair if every node that remains active and eligible from some iteration onward is eventually selected. If processing may leave the same node eligible, fairness requires infinitely many selections of every perpetually eligible node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair selection prevents starvation of persistently eligible active nodes.
assumptions_latex: Eligibility is defined independently of the policy's current tie-breaking choice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\text{ persistently eligible}\Longrightarrow N\text{ is eventually selected}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fair Node Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unrestricted depth-first selection to be fair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In an infinite binary tree, suppose processing each current left descendant creates a deeper active left descendant while a right child R remains active at depth one. A policy choosing the deepest newest node follows the infinite left branch and never selects R.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite descending branch can make pure depth-first search starve another active node forever.
assumptions_latex: The search can generate an infinite branch.
Deepest-node ties favor the newest descendant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{pure depth-first selection}\not\Rightarrow\text{fairness}.

notation.meaning: Active node starved by depth-first selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Depth-First Starvation

children.title: Incumbent Discovery
children.top_down_role: Sources of feasible candidate solutions during global search.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Discovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction and acceptance of improved feasible points during global search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain either no incumbent or a certified feasible pair \((\hat x,U)\) with \(U=f(\hat x)\). From a selected node \(R\), generate candidates by a prescribed sampling, repair, or local-optimization routine. For each candidate \(x\), evaluate the constraints and objective with the validation procedure. If \(x\in X\) is certified and either no incumbent exists or \(f(x)<U\), set \((\hat x,U)\leftarrow(x,f(x))\); otherwise retain the current pair. Stop candidate generation according to its finite budget and return the best validated pair found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate candidates within a search node and replace the incumbent only when a candidate is certified feasible and improves its objective value.
assumptions_latex: Objective comparisons and feasibility acceptance use validated values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever an incumbent is returned, \(\hat x\in X\), \(U=f(\hat x)\), and \(U\) is no larger than any previously accepted incumbent value.

notation.meaning: Search node from which candidates are generated.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Candidate Generation Has No Certificate Force
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of heuristic discovery from certified incumbent acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point returned by sampling, repair, local optimization, rounding, or another primal heuristic changes neither the certified incumbent nor a valid exclusion decision until its feasibility and objective upper bound are validated. Failure of every discovery routine does not imply X=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal heuristics only propose candidates; failure to discover a point proves nothing about feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{candidate proposal}\not\Rightarrow\text{certified incumbent},\qquad\text{no candidate found}\not\Rightarrow X=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Candidate Generation Has No Certificate Force

children.title: Incumbent Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks governing acceptance of candidate solutions as valid incumbents.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal certificate for a candidate to furnish a rigorous primal upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X\}, a candidate \hat x supplies a valid incumbent bound only when \hat x\in X is certified under the declared model and f(\hat x)\leq U is certified. Then p^*\leq U. A tolerance-feasibility certificate instead concerns the tolerance-modified model unless it also implies exact-model feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified feasibility and a rigorous objective upper bound for the same candidate yield an incumbent bound for the same model.
assumptions_latex: The feasibility certificate and objective enclosure concern the same candidate and declared model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \hat x\in X\ \wedge\ f(\hat x)\leq U\Longrightarrow p^*\leq U.

notation.meaning: Global infimum of the declared model.
Certified objective upper bound at the candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Model Incumbent Acceptance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Point or Model Mismatch Invalidates Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for tolerance models, transformed models, and repaired candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Feasibility for a relaxed, tolerance-modified, scaled, or transformed model does not certify original-model feasibility without a sound implication or equivalence. Validation of a repaired point x^r supplies a bound using f(x^r), not the unvalidated objective of the original proposal \hat x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility and objective validation must concern the same point and the same model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^r\in X\not\Rightarrow\hat x\in X.
knowledge_statements.title: Point or Model Mismatch Invalidates Acceptance
Incumbent Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerically rigorous certificate that a candidate supplies a valid global-search upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a candidate \(\hat x\), a validation certificate consists of enclosures \(F
i f(\hat x)\), \(G_i
i g_i(\hat x)\), and \(H_j
i h_j(\hat x)\), computed with directed rounding. It is accepted when \(\sup G_i\leq0\) for every inequality constraint, \(H_j\subseteq[-	au_j,	au_j]\) for every equality constraint under declared tolerances, and all domain constraints are certified. Then \(U:=\sup F\) is recorded as the primal bound. Exact equality feasibility instead requires a separate exact or existence certificate, not merely a floating-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outward-rounded enclosures certify all constraints and provide a safe objective upper bound; small unvalidated residuals alone do not certify exact equalities.
assumptions_latex: Equality tolerances \(\tau_j\geq0\) are explicitly part of the accepted feasibility model.
All displayed enclosures are mathematically guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance certifies tolerance-feasibility of \(\hat x\) and the safe upper bound \(f(\hat x)\leq U\).

notation.meaning: Validated enclosures of the objective, inequalities, and equalities.
Declared tolerance for equality constraint j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate distinguishes tolerance feasibility from exact equality feasibility and is mathematically plausible, but the directed-rounding and enclosure acceptance rules have no cited source.

children.title: Primal-Bound Dissemination
children.top_down_role: Use of incumbent objective values across active subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Bound Dissemination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global propagation of an improved certified incumbent across the active search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a shared certified primal bound \(U\), initially \(+\infty\) if no incumbent exists. When a validated feasible point yields a certified bound \(U'<U\), atomically set \(U\leftarrow U'\) and make the new value available to every active node. For each node \(N\), reapply its cutoff-dependent contraction and fathom it whenever its certified lower bound satisfies \(L(N)\geq U-\varepsilon\). A worker holding a stale bound \(U_{\mathrm{s}}\geq U\) may continue bounding and may fathom only using a certified primal bound it has actually received; using \(U_{\mathrm{s}}\) is safe but can delay exclusions. Dissemination is complete when every active-node or worker view has received the current bound \(U\) or a subsequently improved certified bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broadcast each improved certified upper bound, rerun cutoff-dependent reductions, and prune active nodes whose lower bounds cannot improve the received incumbent beyond tolerance; stale larger bounds remain safe but prune less aggressively.
assumptions_latex: Every disseminated value is a safe objective upper bound obtained from a certified feasible point.
\(L(N)\) is a valid lower bound for node \(N\).
\(\varepsilon\geq0\) is the declared absolute optimality tolerance.
Successive shared primal bounds are nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After a node receives \(U\), the condition \(L(N)\geq U-\varepsilon\) certifies its safe exclusion from the search for an improvement exceeding \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Current shared certified primal upper bound.
Possibly stale certified primal bound held by a worker.
Certified lower bound for node N.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimistic or Unvalidated Broadcast Is Unsafe
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety boundary for values admitted to the dissemination channel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a disseminated value \widetilde U is not certified to satisfy p^*\leq\widetilde U, the test L(N)\geq\widetilde U-\varepsilon can delete a node containing a global optimizer. Underestimated objective values and values from infeasible candidates must therefore not be published as primal bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broadcasting an unvalidated value that is too small can cause unsound pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*>\widetilde U\Longrightarrow\widetilde U\text{ is unsafe for bound-based exclusion}.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimistic or Unvalidated Broadcast Is Unsafe

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering property of asynchronously held certified primal bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let U be the current certified incumbent bound and U_s\geq U an older certified bound. For any valid node lower bound L and \varepsilon\geq0, L\geq U_s-\varepsilon implies L\geq U-\varepsilon. Thus a stale larger bound can delay exclusions but cannot create an exclusion unavailable under U.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale larger certified upper bound is safe but weaker: it can delay pruning, never add pruning.
assumptions_latex: U_s and U are certified primal upper bounds.
L is a valid node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{L:L\geq U_s-\varepsilon\}\subseteq\{L:L\geq U-\varepsilon\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Bound Safety and Dominance

children.title: Certified Subproblem Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for certified removal of subproblems.

children.title: Bound-Based Fathoming
children.top_down_role: Subproblem removal justified by certified objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Based Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe exclusion of a node using certified primal and dual objective bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node \(N\), a bound-fathoming certificate is a pair \((L(N),U)\) such that \(L(N)\leq\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x)\) and \(U=f(\hat x)\) for some certified feasible incumbent \(\hat x\). Given an absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), if \(L(N)\geq U-\varepsilon\), then every \(x\in F_N\) satisfies \(f(x)\geq U-\varepsilon\). Thus the node contains no point improving the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\) and may be removed without affecting the claimed optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node is fathomed when its certified lower bound is no better than the certified incumbent value up to the chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
Both the node lower bound and incumbent feasibility are certified.
\(F_N\) denotes the feasible set within node \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(N)\geq U-\varepsilon\) certifies safe removal of \(N\) from the search for an improvement exceeding \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set restricted to node N.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18
Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18
Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-bound fathoming under an explicitly declared mixed tolerance convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node with certified lower bound L(N) and certified feasible incumbent value U, fix \varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0 and set \tau(U)=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U|\}. If L(N)\ge U-\tau(U), then every feasible point in the node has objective at least U-\tau(U), so the node may be fathomed under this stated convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified lower bound within the declared absolute-plus-scaled-relative tolerance of a feasible incumbent permits safe tolerance-based fathoming.
assumptions_latex: U=f(\hat x) for a certified feasible point \hat x.
The reported tolerance convention is exactly \tau(U).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(N)\ge U-\tau(U) excludes every node improvement larger than \tau(U).

notation.meaning: Declared mixed absolute-relative tolerance at incumbent value U.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Absolute–Relative Fathoming Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure example showing that lower-bound validity is indispensable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min\{x:0\le x\le1\}. The feasible incumbent \hat x=1/2 has U=1/2. If the invalid number L=1 is treated as a node lower bound, the exact test L\ge U removes the entire node although its true minimum is 0<U.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An overestimated node bound can satisfy the pruning inequality and delete the region containing the true optimizer.
assumptions_latex: L=1 is not a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\ge U is safe only when L\le\inf_{x\in F_N}f(x) is certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid-Bound False Fathoming

children.title: Infeasibility Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Removal of regions certified to contain no feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified removal of a node whose feasible intersection is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a node region and \(F\) the global feasible set. An infeasibility-exclusion certificate is any verifiable relaxation or enclosure establishing \(F\cap R=\varnothing\). Sufficient forms include a sound contractor returning the empty set, a constraint range enclosure \(G_i(R)\) with \(\inf G_i(R)>0\) for a required inequality \(g_i(x)\leq0\), or a rigorously infeasible relaxation whose feasible set contains \(F\cap R\). Once such a certificate is obtained, remove \(R\) from the active partition because it contains no feasible optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An empty sound contraction, a violated constraint enclosure, or an infeasible outer relaxation certifies that a node contains no feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Every contractor, range enclosure, or relaxation used is inclusion-valid on \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate establishes \(F\cap R=\varnothing\), so excluding \(R\) cannot remove a feasible global minimizer.

notation.meaning: Certified enclosure of the range of constraint i on R.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Deterministic Global Optimization: Approaches and Classes of Problems p. 18

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Farkas Certificate for an Infeasible Linear Outer System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier certificate for infeasibility of a linear outer relaxation of the regional feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose F\cap R\subseteq\{x:Ax\leq b\}. If y\geq0,\ y^TA=0, and y^Tb<0, then Ax\leq b is infeasible and hence F\cap R=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified Farkas multiplier for an infeasible linear outer relaxation proves regional infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Ax\leq b is an outer relaxation of F\cap R.
The multiplier relations are exact or rigorously validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists y\geq0:\ y^TA=0,\ y^Tb<0\Longrightarrow F\cap R=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Certificate for an Infeasible Linear Outer System

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional infeasibility certified by excluding zero from a required equality range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If feasibility requires h_j(x)=0 and a validated enclosure H_j(R)\supseteq\{h_j(x):x\in R\} satisfies 0\notin H_j(R), then F\cap R=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region is infeasible when a validated range of a required equality excludes zero.
assumptions_latex: H_j(R) contains every value of h_j on R.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\notin H_j(R)\Longrightarrow F\cap R=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Validated range enclosure for equality j on R.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Range Exclusion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between unsuccessful feasibility search and certified regional emptiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Failure of a local solver, an iteration limit, an unvalidated positive residual, or an unsupported infeasible status does not imply F\cap R=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure to find a feasible point is not an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{unsuccessful numerical search}\not\Rightarrow F\cap R=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Feasible portion of the current region.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Failure Is Not Infeasibility

children.title: Dominance Exclusion
children.top_down_role: Removal of regions unable to improve upon an accepted incumbent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional exclusion through certified pointwise domination by retained feasible representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \min\{f(x):x\in F\}, let R be a candidate region and K a region that remains represented in the unresolved search or has already been solved to the claimed tolerance. If for every x\in F\cap R there exists y\in F\cap K with f(y)\le f(x), then \inf_{y\in F\cap K}f(y)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x), and R may be removed without changing the global infimum. A certified map T:F\cap R\to F\cap K satisfying f(Tx)\le f(x) is a sufficient, checkable realization. If only non-strict dominance is known, removal preserves the optimal value but need not preserve every minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region is value-dominated when each feasible point in it has a no-worse feasible representative in a retained or adequately solved region.
assumptions_latex: The pointwise existence relation or sufficient map is certified over all of F\cap R.
K remains represented or has been solved to the claimed tolerance.
The output convention distinguishes preservation of optimal value from preservation of all minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Excluding R preserves the global infimum; non-strict dominance alone does not preserve the full minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.title: Represented-Region Dominance Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when mutually or equally dominating representatives are all discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=\{r,k\}, let R=\{r\}, K=\{k\}, and set f(r)=f(k)=0. Each point is non-strictly dominated by the other. Removing R is sound while K remains represented, but removing K afterward solely by reference to the already removed R leaves no represented feasible point and can make an empty frontier falsely appear to certify infeasibility. Dominance removals therefore require an acyclic retained representative or an adequately solved representative class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal or circular dominance does not justify deleting every representative of an optimal equivalence class.
assumptions_latex: The example uses non-strict pairwise dominance.
No representative is independently solved or retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dominance deletion is unsound when its justification depends only on representatives that are also deleted without independent accounting.
knowledge_statements.title: Circular Dominance Removal Failure
Dominance Exclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Region exclusion through a verifiable mapping to feasible points with no worse objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a candidate region and \(K\) a retained region. A dominance certificate is a verifiable map \(T:F\cap R\to F\cap K\) satisfying \(f(Tx)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\cap R\). If equality is possible, \(K\) must remain represented in the search or already have been solved to the required tolerance. Then every feasible objective value attainable in \(R\) is matched or improved in \(K\), so removing \(R\) preserves the global infimum. Strict inequality additionally certifies that no global minimizer lies exclusively in \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region may be removed when every feasible point in it maps verifiably to a retained feasible point with no larger objective.
assumptions_latex: The mapping \(T\) and its feasibility and objective inequalities are certified over all of \(F\cap R\).
The dominating region \(K\) remains represented or is adequately solved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in F\cap K}f(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)\), so exclusion of \(R\) preserves the global optimal value.

notation.meaning: Certified dominance mapping from feasible points in R to feasible points in K.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mapping-based dominance certificate is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular dominance formulation or its retained-region qualification.

children.title: Certified Region Removal
children.top_down_role: Lifecycle and accounting requirements for safely eliminating search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Region Removal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe exclusion certificate for a minimization subregion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f\) over a feasible set \(F\subseteq X\), with incumbent value \(U=f(\bar x)\) for some \(\bar x\in F\). A region \(R\subseteq X\) may be permanently removed when a valid certificate establishes either \(R\cap F=\varnothing\) or a lower bound \(L(R)\leq\inf_{x\in R\cap F}f(x)\) satisfying \(L(R)\geq U\). Under either condition, removing \(R\) cannot eliminate any feasible point having objective value strictly below \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region is safely discarded if it is infeasible or its certified lower bound is no better than the incumbent value.
assumptions_latex: \(L(R)\) is a valid lower bound on \(R\cap F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) contains no feasible point \(x\) with \(f(x)<U\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for region R

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage and audit conditions making permanent region deletion globally sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D be the original domain, \mathcal A_k the active regions, and \mathcal R_k the removed regions. Maintain F\cap D\subseteq(\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal A_k}A)\cup(\bigcup_{R\in\mathcal R_k}R), and retain for every R\in\mathcal R_k a checkable certificate that F\cap R=\varnothing or f(x)\ge U-\varepsilon for every x\in F\cap R, where U is a certified feasible incumbent value. If \mathcal A_k=\varnothing, all-infeasibility removals certify F\cap D=\varnothing; otherwise the retained certificates certify absolute \varepsilon-global optimality of the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every deleted region must remain represented by an auditable certificate; only exhaustive accounting makes an empty active frontier a global certificate.
assumptions_latex: U=f(\bar x) for a certified feasible incumbent whenever optimality is claimed.
Subdivision children cover the parent's unresolved feasible portion.
Every removed region retains its applicable certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An empty active family supports infeasibility or \varepsilon-optimality only through exhaustive certified accounting.

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Partition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successive subdivision using axis-aligned boxes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rectangular partition method for minimizing \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) on an initial box \(X=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R^n\) maintains finite partitions \(\mathcal P_k\) of \(X\) into axis-aligned boxes with pairwise disjoint interiors. At iteration \(k\), it selects one or more boxes using sampled values, scores, or valid bounds, replaces each selected box by finitely many axis-aligned child boxes whose union equals the parent, and retains the other boxes. Candidate solutions are computed from information attached to boxes in \(\mathcal P_k\); when valid boxwise lower bounds are available, their minimum supplies a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These methods repeatedly partition an initial box into axis-aligned subboxes and use sampled values, scores, or valid bounds to select regions for refinement.
assumptions_latex: \(X=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty compact box.
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is the objective being minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(\mathcal P_k\) is a finite box partition of \(X\), and refinement preserves coverage of \(X\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical exact subdivision variants for an axis-aligned box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For R=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i], a coordinate split chooses j and s\in(\ell_j,u_j), replacing R by the two boxes using [\ell_j,s] and [s,u_j] in coordinate j. Their union is R and their interiors are disjoint. Midpoint longest-side bisection chooses j\in\arg\max_i(u_i-\ell_i) and s=(\ell_j+u_j)/2; every infinite descendant chain generated by this rule has diameter tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate splitting preserves an exact rectangular partition, and repeated longest-side midpoint bisection shrinks every infinite descendant chain.
assumptions_latex: R is a nondegenerate compact axis-aligned box.
For shrinkage, every descendant is bisected at the midpoint of a longest side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R=R^-\cup R^+,\quad\operatorname{int}(R^-)\cap\operatorname{int}(R^+)=\varnothing;\qquad\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonexhaustive Box Selection Can Miss the Global Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition validity alone does not ensure global convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If after some iteration a rectangular method never again refines or samples any active box containing a global minimizer, its sampled set need not approach that minimizer and its incumbent may remain strictly above the global minimum, even for a continuous function on a compact box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid box partition can fail globally when selection permanently ignores every minimizer-containing box.
assumptions_latex: f is continuous on a compact box.
No minimizer-containing active box is sampled or refined after some finite iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Partition validity alone does not imply }U_k\to f^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Axis-aligned rectangular partition through a coordinate hyperplane
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a rectangle and its binary coordinate-aligned subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rectangle in \(\mathbb R^n\) is \(M=[r,s]=\prod_{i=1}^n[r_i,s_i]=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:r_i\le x_i\le s_i,\ i=1,\ldots,n\}\). Given \(v\in M\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the partition via \((v,j)\) consists of \(M_-=\{x:r_j\le x_j\le v_j,\ r_i\le x_i\le s_i\ (i\ne j)\}\) and \(M_+=\{x:v_j\le x_j\le s_j,\ r_i\le x_i\le s_i\ (i\ne j)\}\), determined by the hyperplane \(x_j=v_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An axis-aligned rectangle is a Cartesian product of closed coordinate intervals. Choosing a point in it and a coordinate splits it into two subrectangles along the coordinate hyperplane through that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M=M_-\cup M_+\), with \(M_-\cap M_+=\{x\in M:x_j=v_j\}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic multidimensional rectangular-partition global-search scheme driven by a partition operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with $I_0=\{0\}$ and $D_0=[a,b]$, evaluate $f$ at the lower-left and upper-right vertices and optionally at finitely many additional points. At iteration $k$, each current box $D_i=[x_i^l,x_i^u]$, $i\in I_k$, has samples including those two vertices and may receive finitely many further samples. Compute $P_i\{D_i,f(D_i)\}$, choose any $t\in I_k$ attaining the maximum operator value, and replace $D_t$ at its prescribed central point by two equal-volume half-boxes $D_{t+1}$ and $D_{t+2}$. Set $I_{k+1}=(I_k\cup\{t+1,t+2\})\setminus\{t\}$ and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with the original box and finitely many function evaluations. At each iteration, compute a partition-operator score for every current box, select any maximizing box, split it at the prescribed center into two equal-volume boxes, update the partition, and repeat.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_t\text{ is replaced by two equal-volume half-boxes and }I_{k+1}=(I_k\cup\{t+1,t+2\})\setminus\{t\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Partition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successive subdivision using simplices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A simplicial partition method for minimizing \(f\) on a compact polytope \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) maintains finite families \(\mathcal T_k\) of nondegenerate simplices whose union is \(X\) and whose interiors are pairwise disjoint. At each iteration, selected simplices are replaced by finitely many simplicial children forming an exact subdivision of each parent, commonly by edge bisection or insertion of a new vertex. Function values, relaxations, or lower bounds associated with simplices determine refinement and incumbent updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These methods cover the domain by simplices, select promising simplices, and replace them with exact simplicial subdivisions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a compact polytope admitting a finite triangulation.
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is the objective being minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every refinement produces a finite simplicial partition \(\mathcal T_{k+1}\) covering the same domain \(X\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact simplex subdivision through an edge midpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\} be nondegenerate and let m=(v_i+v_j)/2 lie on an edge [v_i,v_j]. With V=\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}, define S_i=\operatorname{conv}((V\setminus\{v_i\})\cup\{m\}) and S_j=\operatorname{conv}((V\setminus\{v_j\})\cup\{m\}). Then S=S_i\cup S_j and their interiors are disjoint. A conforming triangulation may require compatible bisection of neighbors sharing the edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge-midpoint bisection produces two exact simplicial children; neighboring simplices may require compatible refinement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=S_i\cup S_j,\qquad\operatorname{int}(S_i)\cap\operatorname{int}(S_j)=\varnothing.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coverage alone does not guarantee useful refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact simplicial partitions need not yield global convergence if minimizer-containing descendants are ignored or have diameter bounded away from zero. Degenerate simplices also invalidate full-dimensional barycentric or affine-interpolation formulas requiring affinely independent vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid triangulations can fail when relevant simplices do not shrink, while degenerate cells break full-dimensional affine models.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_k\operatorname{diam}(S_k)>0\Longrightarrow\text{convergence is not guaranteed};\qquad\operatorname{affdim}(S)<n\Longrightarrow\text{full-dimensional barycentric models are singular}.

knowledge_statements.title: Conical Partition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successive search through cone-shaped cells or coverings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conical partition method represents a search domain \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) by a finite family \(\mathcal C_k\) of cells obtained from convex cones, typically intersections \(X\cap(v+K)\) of \(X\) with translated cones. The cells cover the active domain and have disjoint interiors when they form a partition. At each iteration, selected conical cells are subdivided or replaced by a finer conical cover, while valid cellwise bounds or sampled objective values control selection and exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These methods cover or partition the search domain with cone-derived cells and progressively refine selected cells using bounds or evaluations.
assumptions_latex: Each generating cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex and has nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active cells in \(\mathcal C_k\) cover every search point not already validly excluded.

children.title: Successive Approximation Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General global-optimization architecture based on successively strengthened relaxations rather than problem subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A successive approximation algorithm starts from an initial relaxation and successively improves it without subdividing the given optimization problem into subproblems as in branch-and-bound. During the iterations it generates lower bounds \(L_k\) and upper bounds \(U_k\) that converge to the optimal value \(v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A successive approximation algorithm repeatedly improves an initial relaxation without subdividing the problem as branch-and-bound does. Its lower and upper bounds converge to the optimal value.
assumptions_latex: \text{The optimization problem has an optimal value }v^*.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\le v^*\le U_k,\qquad L_k\to v^*,\quad U_k\to v^*.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer Approximation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successively tightened supersets of a feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimizing \(f\) over a feasible set \(F\subseteq X\), an outer approximation method constructs tractable sets \(O_k\) satisfying \(F\subseteq O_k\subseteq X\). Refinement adds valid constraints so that \(O_{k+1}\subseteq O_k\), while preserving \(F\subseteq O_{k+1}\). Solving or bounding the relaxation over \(O_k\) yields a lower bound on \(\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\); feasible trial points provide upper bounds. Termination may occur when infeasibility is certified or the upper–lower bound gap meets a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer approximation repeatedly tightens tractable supersets of the feasible set while preserving feasibility and deriving relaxation lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: Every added constraint is valid for all points of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq O_{k+1}\subseteq O_k\), and \(\inf_{x\in O_k}f(x)\leq\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tests based on containment of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F\subseteq O\subseteq X. If x_O\in\arg\min_{x\in O}f(x) and x_O\in F, then x_O is globally optimal over F. If O=\varnothing, then F=\varnothing. For any \bar x\in F, \inf_{x\in O}f(x)\leq f^*\leq f(\bar x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible optimizer of an outer relaxation is globally optimal, while an empty outer relaxation certifies original infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation minimum is attained when the optimizer test is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_O\in F\Longrightarrow f(x_O)=\min_{x\in F}f(x);\qquad O=\varnothing\Longrightarrow F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Relaxation Optimality and Infeasibility Tests

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-step correctness and asymptotic exactness require distinct invariants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If F\nsubseteq O_k, minimizing over O_k need not give a lower bound over F. Even if every O_k contains F, convergence can fail when O_\infty=\bigcap_kO_k strictly contains F; then \min_{O_\infty}f<f^* is possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Containment is required for valid bounds, while removal of all residual infeasible points is required for generic asymptotic exactness.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\nsubseteq O_k\Longrightarrow\text{bound validity may fail};\qquad F\subsetneq O_\infty\Longrightarrow\lim_kL_k<f^*\text{ is possible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Containment and Limit-Exactness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Setwise convergence of compact nested outer descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X be compact, f:X\to\mathbb R continuous, and O_0\supseteq O_1\supseteq\cdots nonempty compact sets with F\subseteq O_k and \bigcap_{k\geq0}O_k=F\neq\varnothing. If L_k=\min_{x\in O_k}f(x), then L_k\uparrow\min_{x\in F}f(x), and every accumulation point of relaxation minimizers is globally minimizing over F.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact nested outer sets whose intersection is exactly the feasible set yield convergent relaxation bounds for continuous objectives.
assumptions_latex: Each O_k is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\uparrow f^*,\qquad \operatorname{acc}\{x^k:x^k\in\arg\min_{O_k}f\}\subseteq\arg\min_Ff.

notation.meaning: minimum over the kth outer approximation

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Outer-Approximation Limit Exactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract iterative procedure under assumptions A1 and A2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(P_1\in\mathcal P\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(x^k=x(P_k)\). If it does not exist, terminate with \(\Omega=\varnothing\). If \(x^k\in G\), terminate with \(x^k\in\Omega\). Otherwise, construct an affine \(l_k\) such that \(l_k(x^k)>0\), \(l_k(x)\leq0\) for all \(x\in G\), and \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\{x\mid l_k(x)\leq0\}\in\mathcal P\); increment \(k\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from an admissible outer set and compute its distinguished point. Absence of that point certifies an empty solution set; a point in the target set is a solution. Otherwise, strictly separate the point from the target set, refine the outer set with the cut, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure either certifies }\Omega=\varnothing,\text{ returns }x^k\in\Omega,\text{ or produces }P_{k+1}\in\mathcal P\text{ with }G\subseteq\{l_k\leq0\}\text{ and }l_k(x^k)>0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of an Infinite Outer-Approximation Procedure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of asymptotic convergence for the abstract OA procedure. The extract's eventual-proximity assertion requires a compactness condition to avoid vacuous convergence when the sequence has no accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An infinite OA procedure generating \(\{x^k\}\) is called convergent if every accumulation point \(\bar x\) of \(\{x^k\}\) belongs to \(G\). Under A1, every such accumulation point belongs to \(\Omega\). If, additionally, \(\{x^k\}\) is relatively compact, then \(\operatorname{dist}(x^k,G)\to0\), so every fixed positive proximity tolerance is eventually met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite OA procedure is convergent when all accumulation points of its distinguished points lie in the target set and hence, under A1, are solutions. Eventual proximity to the target follows when the sequence is relatively compact; it does not follow from the definition alone if there are no accumulation points.

\{x^k\}\text{ is relatively compact for the eventual-proximity conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{acc}\{x^k\}\subseteq G;\qquad \operatorname{acc}\{x^k\}\subseteq\Omega\text{ under A1};\qquad \operatorname{dist}(x^k,G)\to0\text{ under relative compactness}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric sufficient conditions for convergence of an abstract OA sequence generated by strict affine separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed with nonempty interior. Let \(\{x^k\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be an infinite bounded sequence, and let \(l_k(x)=\langle p^k,x\rangle+\alpha_k\) satisfy \(l_k(x^k)>0\) and \(l_k(x)\leq0\) for every \(x\in G\). Suppose that for every \(k\) there exist \(w^k\in G\) and \(y^k\in[w^k,x^k]\setminus\operatorname{int}G\) such that \(l_k(y^k)\geq0\), that \(\{w^k\}\) is bounded, and that every accumulation point of \(\{w^k\}\) belongs to \(\operatorname{int}G\). Then \(x^k-y^k\to0\). In particular, if every accumulation point of \(\{y^k\}\) belongs to \(G\), the OA procedure converges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed target set with nonempty interior, the stated boundedness, strict-separation, segment-point, and interior-accumulation conditions force the OA points and the segment points to coalesce. If every accumulation point of the segment points lies in the target set, the OA procedure converges.
assumptions_latex: l_k(x)=\langle p^k,x\rangle+\alpha_k,\quad l_k(x^k)>0,\quad l_k(x)\leq0\ \forall x\in G
\{w^k\}\text{ is bounded and every accumulation point of }\{w^k\}\text{ lies in }\operatorname{int}G

knowledge_statements.title: Successive Underestimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone strengthening of global objective underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimizing \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), a successive underestimation method constructs tractable functions \(m_k:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(m_k(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). New evaluations or valid inequalities strengthen the model, commonly so that \(m_{k+1}(x)\geq m_k(x)\) for all \(x\). The master value \(L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\) is a global lower bound, while evaluated feasible points supply an upper bound; refinement continues until their gap meets the stopping tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive underestimation builds increasingly strong global lower models whose minima are certified lower bounds on the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), and pointwise strengthening implies \(L_{k+1}\geq L_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Validity Without Tightening Does Not Ensure Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound validity does not imply eventual exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Global validity m_k\leq f guarantees only L_k\leq f^*. For c>0, the constant sequence m_k=f-c is globally valid but satisfies L_k=f^*-c for every k, so the lower bounds never converge to f^*.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid underestimator can remain permanently loose; validity alone does not imply convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_k=f-c\Longrightarrow L_k=f^*-c\not\to f^*.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient convergence condition independent of the model construction.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly accurate valid lower models force their minima and the true values at model minimizers to approach the global optimum.
assumptions_latex: m_k(x)\leq f(x) for every x\in X.
Each m_k attains its infimum for the minimizer conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^*-\delta_k\leq L_k\leq f^*,\qquad f(x^k)\leq f^*+\delta_k.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Annexation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progressive enlargement of a polyhedral approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polyhedral annexation method constructs a nested sequence of polyhedral sets \(P_k\subseteq X\) by adjoining finitely generated polyhedral pieces: \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cup Q_k\), where \(Q_k\subseteq X\) and the union is represented or decomposed polyhedrally. Each annexed piece is selected from information obtained by optimizing, separating, or evaluating outside \(P_k\). The method uses the growing covered region to update bounds or incumbent solutions and seeks coverage sufficient to certify the global optimum or the prescribed optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral annexation progressively enlarges a polyhedrally represented region by adding selected polyhedral pieces and updating global bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k\subseteq P_{k+1}\subseteq X\) for every iteration \(k\).

children.title: Global Cutting-Plane Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Global Cutting-Plane Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master relaxation refined by globally valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be minimized over \(F\), and choose a relaxation \(R_0\) satisfying \(F\subseteq R_0\subseteq X\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(L_k=\inf\{f(x):x\in R_k\}\) and obtain a minimizer \(x^k\). If \(x^k\in F\), return \(x^k\), which is globally optimal over \(F\). Otherwise, use a separation oracle to obtain a cut \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_k\) that is satisfied by every \(x\in F\) and violated by \(x^k\), and set \(R_{k+1}=R_k\cap\{x\in X:a_k^{\mathsf T}x\leq b_k\}\). Repeat until a feasible master minimizer is found or infeasibility is certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pure global cutting-plane method solves a relaxation and, whenever its minimizer is infeasible, adds a globally valid inequality that removes that minimizer without removing any feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is the objective minimized over \(F\).
Each master problem attains its infimum.
For every infeasible master minimizer, the oracle supplies a cut valid on \(F\) and violated by that minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxations satisfy \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\), and any returned feasible master minimizer is globally optimal over \(F\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate from the relaxation bound and a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F\subseteq R_k, let L_k=\inf_{x\in R_k}f(x), and let \bar x^k\in F with U_k=f(\bar x^k). Then L_k\leq f^*\leq U_k, where f^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x). Hence U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon certifies f(\bar x^k)-f^*\leq\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master lower bound and a feasible incumbent bracket the global optimum, so their gap certifies global accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\leq f^*\leq U_k,\qquad U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\Longrightarrow f(\bar x^k)-f^*\leq\varepsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity and Separation Are Both Essential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsafe cuts can destroy correctness; nonseparating cuts can cause stalling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For R_{k+1}=R_k\cap H_k, if F\nsubseteq H_k, the update can exclude a global optimizer and the master value need not remain a lower bound. If H_k is valid on F but x^k\in H_k for the current infeasible master minimizer x^k, the same point may remain optimal and progress is not ensured.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalid cuts can destroy global correctness, while valid cuts that do not separate the current infeasible optimizer can cause stalling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\nsubseteq H_k\Longrightarrow\text{correctness may fail};\qquad x^k\in H_k\Longrightarrow\text{progress is not ensured}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact termination under an exhaustive finite separating family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a finite family \mathcal H of inequalities is valid for F, and every infeasible master minimizer violates an unused member of \mathcal H. If every iteration adds such a member and each nonempty master problem attains its minimum, then after at most |\mathcal H| nonterminal additions the method finds a feasible master minimizer or obtains an empty master relaxation. The former is globally optimal and the latter certifies F=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exhaustive finite separating family gives finite termination because every failed iteration permanently consumes a new cut.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \mathcal H is valid on F.
Every infeasible master minimizer violates an unused member of \mathcal H.
Every nonempty master problem is solved globally and attains its optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{cut}}\leq|\mathcal H|,\text{ followed by global optimality or certified infeasibility}.

knowledge_statements.title: Piyavskii–Shubert Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Univariate Lipschitz search by a piecewise-conical lower envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) be Lipschitz with known constant \(L>0\), and fix a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\). From sampled points \(x_i\) and values \(f_i=f(x_i)\), form \(m_k(x)=\max_i\{f_i-L|x-x_i|\}\), which globally underestimates \(f\). Initialize with endpoint samples, choose \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[a,b]}m_k(x)\), evaluate \(f(x^{k+1})\), and update the envelope. Let \(\bar x_k\) be a sampled point with incumbent value \(U_k=f(\bar x_k)\). Stop when \(U_k-\min_{x\in[a,b]}m_k(x)\leq\varepsilon\), and return \(\bar x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method minimizes a Lipschitz lower envelope, samples at its minimizer, and returns the best sampled point once the certified lower-bound gap is at most the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(f(\bar x_k)-\min_{x\in[a,b]}f(x)\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Lipschitz lower envelope after the current samples

knowledge_statements.title: Multivariate Lipschitz Partition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-partition search using multivariate Lipschitz lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz on a compact box \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) under a norm \(\|\cdot\|\), and fix \(\varepsilon\geq0\). Maintain a finite box partition \(\mathcal P_k\) of \(X\). For every \(R\in\mathcal P_k\), choose a sampled representative \(c_R\in R\) and compute \(B(R)=f(c_R)-L\max_{x\in R}\|x-c_R\|\). Select one or more boxes having the smallest bounds, subdivide them, and evaluate representatives of the new boxes. Let \(\bar x_k\) be the best sampled point and let \(U_k=f(\bar x_k)\). Stop when \(U_k-\min_{R\in\mathcal P_k}B(R)\leq\varepsilon\), and return \(\bar x_k\) with the partition-based lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method partitions a box, gives every subbox a Lipschitz lower bound, and refines boxes with the smallest bounds until the certified gap is at most the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty compact box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(f(\bar x_k)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: valid Lipschitz lower bound for box R

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invalidity Under an Underestimated Lipschitz Constant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between a heuristic search score and a certified regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sampled representative \(c_R\in R\), the expression \(f(c_R)-\widehat L\max_{x\in R}\|x-c_R\|\) is guaranteed to lower-bound \(\min_{x\in R}f(x)\) when \(\widehat L\) is a valid Lipschitz constant on \(R\). If \(\widehat L\) is smaller than the least valid regional Lipschitz modulus, the expression need not be a lower bound; pruning or termination based on it can therefore remove a global minimizer or produce a false gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An underestimated Lipschitz constant may guide search but cannot safely support pruning or certified termination.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat L\) has not been proved to be a valid regional Lipschitz constant.

knowledge_statements.title: Invalidity Under an Underestimated Lipschitz Constant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative convergence of valid-bound multivariate Lipschitz partitions under exhaustive spatial refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz on a compact box \(X\). For each finite partition \(\mathcal P_k\), sample \(c_R\in R\) and set \(r_R=\max_{x\in R}\|x-c_R\|\), \(\rho_k=\max_R r_R\), \(U_k=\min_R f(c_R)\), and \(L_k=\min_R\{f(c_R)-Lr_R\}\). Then \(L_k\leq f^*\leq U_k\) and \(0\leq U_k-L_k\leq L\rho_k\). Consequently, if \(\rho_k\to0\), then \(L_k\to f^*\) and \(U_k\to f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid Lipschitz partition bounds have gap at most the Lipschitz constant times the maximum cell radius, so vanishing radius yields convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\leq U_k-L_k\leq L\rho_k;\qquad \rho_k\to0\Longrightarrow L_k,U_k\to f^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absence of a Lipschitz Gap Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate boundary for classical potentially-optimal selection without a validated regularity modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finite DIRECT data \(\{(c_i,f(c_i),d_i)\}_{i=1}^N\) and selection over hypothetical slopes \(K>0\) do not by themselves provide a certified global lower bound for an arbitrary continuous objective. Without an independently valid modulus of continuity, any finite sample set leaving a nonempty open region unsampled is compatible with a continuous function having the same sampled values and an arbitrarily deep well in that region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hypothetical Lipschitz slopes guide DIRECT selection but do not certify a finite global optimality gap without independently validated regularity information.

The objective is continuous, but no valid modulus of continuity is known.

DIRECT-Type Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Potentially optimal rectangle selection over implicit Lipschitz slopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After scaling a compact box to \([0,1]^n\), maintain rectangles \(R_i\) with centers \(c_i\), center values \(f_i=f(c_i)\), and size measures \(d_i\). Given incumbent \(f_{\min}\) and parameter \(\epsilon\geq0\), declare \(R_i\) potentially optimal if some \(K>0\) satisfies \(f_i-Kd_i\leq f_j-Kd_j\) for every \(j\) and \(f_i-Kd_i\leq f_{\min}-\epsilon|f_{\min}|\). Subdivide every potentially optimal rectangle along its longest dimensions, sample new centers, and repeat until a stated evaluation, size, or accuracy stopping rule is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DIRECT selects rectangles that are best for some positive Lipschitz slope, subdivides them along longest dimensions, and does not fix one global constant.
assumptions_latex: The search domain is a nonempty compact box rescaled to \([0,1]^n\).
The objective is evaluated at rectangle centers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected rectangles lie on the lower convex envelope of the points \((d_i,f_i)\) under the stated sufficient-decrease test.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fair Coarse-Cell Refinement Implies Global Value Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic convergence theorem for center-sampled rectangular partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[0,1]^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. Consider finite rectangular partitions \(\mathcal P_k\) in which every created rectangle is sampled at its center. Assume there is \(q<1\) such that every child of a refined rectangle has diameter at most \(q\) times its parent's diameter, and assume every persistent rectangle above each fixed positive diameter threshold is eventually refined. Then the mesh tends to zero, the sampled centers are dense, and the incumbent values converge to \(\min f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform contraction and fair refinement of every persistent coarse cell imply dense center sampling and global value convergence.
assumptions_latex: Every created rectangle is sampled at its center.
Child diameters contract by a common factor \(q<1\).
Every persistent rectangle above every fixed positive diameter threshold is eventually refined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{R\in\mathcal P_k}\operatorname{diam}(R)\to0,\quad \overline{\{c_j:j\ge1\}}=[0,1]^n,\quad U_k\to\min f.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Partition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box refinement driven by information at diagonal endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a compact box and maintain a partition \(\mathcal P_k\) into boxes \(R=[u_R,v_R]\). Evaluate or reuse objective values at diagonal endpoints \(u_R,v_R\), and assign each box a score or valid lower bound \(B(R)\) derived from these values, the diagonal length \(\|v_R-u_R\|\), and any assumed variation bound. Select boxes according to \(B(R)\), subdivide them by a prescribed diagonal partition rule, reuse shared endpoint evaluations, and stop under a declared bound-gap, box-size, or evaluation-budget criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal partition methods score boxes using their diagonal endpoints and lengths, then subdivide selected boxes while reusing endpoint evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty compact box.
Whenever global certification is claimed, \(B(R)\leq\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\) for every active box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If stopped with \(U_k-\min_{R\in\mathcal P_k}B(R)\leq\varepsilon\), the incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prototype spatial search using an ordered box list, bisection, certified deletion, and certified contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the ordered list with the initial box, \(L=\{X\}\). Repeatedly bisect the first box into \(V_1\) and \(V_2\). Delete any \(V_i\) proven to contain no solution; diminish any \(V_i\) when a portion is proven to contain no solution; and reinsert each surviving whole or diminished box into \(L\). Stop when the termination criterion holds, and otherwise repeat.
