knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be an inclusion-isotonic interval extension of \(f\), so that \(f(X)=\{f(x):x\in X\}\subseteq F(X)=[\underline F(X),\overline F(X)]\). For the minimization of \(f\) over \(D\), define \(L(X)=\underline F(X)\). If \(D\cap X\ne\varnothing\), then \(L(X)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\cap X\), and consequently \(L(X)\le\inf_{x\in D\cap X}f(x)\). Constraint-derived interval bounds may replace \(L(X)\) only when they preserve this inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower endpoint of a valid interval enclosure of the objective is a rigorous lower bound for every feasible point in the box.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tightening and limiting behavior of lower endpoints from an inclusion-isotonic, convergent interval extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be an inclusion-isotonic interval extension of \(f\), and define \(L(X)=\underline F(X)\). If \(Y\subseteq X\), then \(F(Y)\subseteq F(X)\) and hence \(L(Y)\ge L(X)\). If \(X_{k+1}\subseteq X_k\), \(\bigcap_kX_k=\{x^*\}\), and \(\operatorname{wid}F(X_k)\to0\), then \(L(X_k)\) increases to \(f(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inclusion-isotonic interval lower bound cannot weaken on a nested subbox, and a convergent enclosure approaches the point value on boxes shrinking to a point.
assumptions_latex: F(X) encloses \{f(x):x\in X\} for every relevant box X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y\subseteq X\Longrightarrow L(Y)\ge L(X),\qquad L(X_k)\nearrow f(x^*).

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the value of a known feasible point in a minimization problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A box \(X\) may be fathomed if either of two verifiable conditions holds. First, if \(L(X)\ge U\), no feasible point in \(X\) improves the incumbent value \(U\). Second, if an interval evaluation of some required constraint proves violation throughout \(X\), then \(D\cap X=\varnothing\). Removing any box satisfying either condition cannot remove a feasible point with objective value strictly below \(U\). Equality fathoming is valid when only one global minimizer, rather than all minimizers, must be retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard a box when its certified lower bound cannot beat the incumbent or interval constraint tests prove that the box contains no feasible point.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box can be discarded when its certified lower bound is within the requested absolute tolerance of the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(L(X)\) is a rigorous lower bound on \(D\cap X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(X)\geq U-\varepsilon\Longrightarrow f(x)\geq U-\varepsilon\quad\forall x\in D\cap X.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each active box \(X\), compute \(Y=C(X)\). If \(Y=\varnothing\), fathom \(X\). Otherwise replace \(X\) by \(Y\), recompute interval constraint and objective enclosures on \(Y\), apply the bound and infeasibility fathoming tests, and branch only if \(Y\) survives. Because \(D\cap X\subseteq C(X)\subseteq X\), contraction deletes no feasible point. Reapplying contractors after branching or bound tightening is permitted until no material reduction occurs or a prescribed contraction limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contract every active box before rebounding and branching. Empty contractions are discarded, while nonempty contractions preserve all feasible points and reduce subsequent interval work.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval Newton Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued interval Newton contraction for square nonlinear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use a verified interval linear solver to compute a box \([V]\) containing every vector \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) for which \(Av=F(x_0)\) for some \(A\in[J](X)\). Define \(N(X,x_0)=x_0-[V]\) and \(X^+=X\cap N(X,x_0)\). Then every zero of \(F\) in \(X\) belongs to \(X^+\). Return \(X^+\) as the contracted box; if \(X^+=\varnothing\), return an exclusion result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enclose every solution of the interval Newton linear system and intersect its translated image with the original box. The resulting subbox retains every zero, and an empty intersection excludes all zeros.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuously differentiable on the box \(X\).
\(x_0\in X\), and \([J](X)\) encloses \(F'(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
The verified interval linear solver encloses the united solution set of \(Av=F(x_0)\) over all \(A\in[J](X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^*)=0\) and \(x^*\in X\) imply \(x^*\in X^+=X\cap N(X,x_0)\subseteq X\).

notation.meaning: Interval enclosure of the Jacobians on the box.
Verified enclosure of the united interval-linear-system solution set.
Contracted box obtained by intersection with the Newton image.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point-preconditioned contraction variant for square nonlinear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a box \(X\), center \(x_0\in X\), point matrix \(C\), and validated Jacobian enclosure \([J](X)\), compute \(K(X)=x_0-CF(x_0)+(I-C[J](X))(X-x_0)\) with outward rounding and set \(X^+=X\cap K(X)\). Every zero of \(F\) in \(X\) belongs to \(X^+\). Thus a nonempty \(X^+\) is a solution-preserving contraction and an empty \(X^+\) excludes every zero from \(X\). The operation may be repeated after recomputing enclosures on the contracted box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect the box with its verified Krawczyk image to preserve all roots while contracting the box; an empty intersection excludes roots.
assumptions_latex: C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n} is fixed and all interval operations use outward rounding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x\in X:F(x)=0\}\subseteq X^+=X\cap K(X)\subseteq X.

knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krawczyk interior-inclusion certificate for existence and uniqueness of a zero under a verified contraction condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(K(X)=x_0-CF(x_0)+(I-C[J](X))(X-x_0)\) using outward-rounded interval arithmetic. Verify an induced-norm bound \(\sup_{B\in I-C[J](X)}\lVert B\rVert\le q<1\). If also \(K(X)\subset\operatorname{int}(X)\), then \(F\) has exactly one zero in \(X\). The certificate records \(X\), \(x_0\), \(C\), \(F(x_0)\), \([J](X)\), the computed image \(K(X)\), the norm bound \(q\), and the directed-rounding mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly interior Krawczyk image together with a verified contraction bound certifies that the nonlinear system has exactly one zero in the box.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuously differentiable on the box \(X\).
\(x_0\in\operatorname{int}(X)\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \([J](X)\) encloses \(F'(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
For an induced matrix norm, \(\sup_{B\in I-C[J](X)}\lVert B\rVert\le q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(X)\subset\operatorname{int}(X)\) implies that \(F\) has exactly one zero in \(X\).

If \(N(X,x_0)\subset\operatorname{int}(X)\), then \(F\) has exactly one zero in \(X\), and that zero lies in \(\operatorname{int}(X)\).

children.title: Singular-Jacobian Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where derivative enclosures limit contraction or certification.

assumptions_latex: The interval Newton step uses the derivative enclosure \(F'(X)=[-2r,2r]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Because \(0\in F'(X)\) and \(F'(0)=0\), regular interval Newton inversion and simple-root uniqueness certification fail on \(X\).

notation.meaning: Scalar residual map with a multiple zero.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Algorithms Based on Interval Methods p. 46

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=x^2\) and \(X=[-r,r]\) with \(r>0\). The unique zero \(x^*=0\) is multiple, and the interval derivative is \(F'(X)=[-2r,2r]\), which contains the singular value \(0\). Consequently, an interval Newton formula requiring division by \(F'(X)\) is not a regular contraction, and an interior-inclusion test designed to certify a simple zero cannot establish simple-root uniqueness at \(x^*\). Subdivision alone does not remove the singularity from every box containing \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the multiple root of x squared, every enclosing interval derivative contains zero, so regular interval Newton inversion and simple-root certification break down.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Jacobian Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete enclosure-overestimation example distinguishing failure to verify uniform regularity from an actual singular Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(u,v)=(e^u\cos v,e^u\sin v)\) on \(X=[-\delta,\delta]\times[0,2\pi]\), where \(\delta>0\). Then \(\det F'(u,v)=e^{2u}>0\) at every point of \(X\), but the natural entrywise interval enclosure of \(F'(X)\) contains the zero matrix and hence singular matrices. Therefore failure to verify regularity of this interval hull does not imply a singular realized Jacobian; Newton tests requiring a uniformly regular enclosure are merely inconclusive. Subdivision or a sharper structured enclosure may restore certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Jacobian can be nonsingular everywhere even though its entrywise interval hull contains singular matrices, making regular Newton tests inconclusive through overestimation alone.
assumptions_latex: [J](X) is the natural entrywise interval enclosure of F'(X).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \det F'(u,v)>0\ \forall(u,v)\in X,\qquad 0_{2\times2}\in[J](X).

notation.meaning: Entrywise interval enclosure of the Jacobian family.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(X^0\) to the current domain box. At iteration \(k\), select a constraint index \(i_k\) and set \(X^{k+1}=C_{i_k}(X^k)\). Whenever a coordinate interval shrinks, reschedule every contractor depending on that coordinate. Stop when \(X^k=\varnothing\), when a full scheduled pass causes no representable change, or when a prescribed reduction tolerance is met. Since each \(C_i\) is contracting and solution-preserving, \(D\cap X^0\subseteq X^{k+1}\subseteq X^k\) for every \(k\). Return the final box and the applied-contractor log.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly apply solution-preserving constraint contractors, rescheduling affected constraints after reductions. The boxes shrink monotonically while retaining every jointly feasible point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Componentwise Propagation from Bounds on a Sum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termwise domain reduction for a separable sum constraint over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $B$ be a box and let $p_1,\ldots,p_t$ be real-valued functions on $B$. For each $k\in\{1,\ldots,t\}$: if $\sum_{j=1}^t p_j(x)\ge c$, $p_j(x)\le\bar p_j$ for every $j$ and $x\in B$, and $\bar c\ge\sum_{j=1}^t\bar p_j$, then $p_k(x)\ge c-\bar c+\bar p_k$. Similarly, if $\sum_{j=1}^t p_j(x)\le c$, $\widehat p_j\le p_j(x)$ for every $j$ and $x\in B$, and $\widehat c\le\sum_{j=1}^t\widehat p_j$, then $p_k(x)\le c-\widehat c+\widehat p_k$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For points satisfying a sum constraint, bounds on all summands imply a valid bound on each individual summand.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial polyblock \(P_0\supseteq G\). At iteration \(k\), select a proper vertex \(v^k\) maximizing \(f\), project it radially to \(y^k\in\partial^+G\), and update the incumbent when \(y^k\in H\). Replace \(v^k\) by the vertices \(v^k-(v_i^k-y_i^k)e_i\), discard dominated or infeasible vertices, and obtain \(P_{k+1}\supseteq G\). Stop when the best remaining vertex value exceeds the incumbent value by at most \(\varepsilon\); return the incumbent as an \(\varepsilon\)-global maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer polyblocks shrink around the normal feasible set. Vertex objective values give upper bounds, while feasible radial projections update the incumbent until the gap is small.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-approximation procedure for problem (MO), subject to its standing order and feasibility assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P_1=[a,b]\). Given a polyblock \(P_k\supseteq G\) with proper vertex set \(T_k\), set \(T'_k=T_k\cap H\). If \(T'_k=\varnothing\), stop and declare infeasibility. Otherwise choose \(z^k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in T'_k}f(x)\). If \(z^k\in G\), return \(z^k\) as an optimal solution of \((\mathrm{MO})\). If \(z^k\notin G\), compute \(x^k=\pi_G(z^k)\) and set \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\bigl([a,b]\setminus(x^k,b]\bigr)\). Then \(G\subseteq P_{k+1}\subseteq P_k\setminus\{z^k\}\), and the procedure is repeated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the bounding box, maximize the increasing objective over the proper vertices that lie in H. An empty such vertex set gives the algorithm's infeasibility stopping condition. A selected vertex in G is optimal; otherwise its projection onto G defines a smaller outer polyblock that retains G and removes the selected vertex.
assumptions_latex: P_k\supseteq G\text{ is a polyblock with proper vertex set }T_k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\subseteq P_{k+1}\subseteq P_k\setminus\{z^k\}\text{, with the stated infeasibility and optimality stopping rules}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the POA monotonic-optimization setting, after shifting the origin to \(-\alpha e\) if necessary, one may assume \[x\leq a+\alpha e\qquad\forall x\in H,\] where \(\alpha>0\) is chosen not too small relative to \(\|b-a\|\), for example \(\alpha=\tfrac14\|b-a\|\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-polyblock reduction algorithm for monotonic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a polyblock \(P_1\supseteq G\cap H\) with proper vertex set \(V_1\), together with an available feasible incumbent \(\bar x^1\) and \(CBV=f(\bar x^1)\); use \(CBV=-\infty\) if no feasible point is known. At iteration \(k\), form \(\bar P_k=\operatorname{red}_{CBV}P_k\) and \(\bar V_k=\operatorname{pvert}(\bar P_k)\). If \(\bar V_k=\varnothing\), declare infeasibility when \(CBV=-\infty\), and otherwise return the incumbent as optimal. Otherwise reset \(b=\bigvee\bar V_k\), choose \(z^k\in\arg\max\{f(x):x\in\bar V_k\}\), and return \(z^k\) as optimal if \(g(z^k)\leq0\). If not, compute \(x^k=\pi_G(z^k)\), update the feasible incumbent and \(CBV\), set \(P_{k+1}=\bar P_k\setminus(x^k,b]\), compute its proper vertices by the polyblock vertex-update rule, increment \(k\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an outer polyblock and an optional feasible incumbent, repeatedly reduce the polyblock, select its objective-maximizing proper vertex, apply the stated termination tests, and otherwise project the vertex onto G, update the incumbent, remove the resulting upper orthant, and recompute the proper vertices.
assumptions_latex: P_1\supseteq G\cap H\text{ is a polyblock with proper vertex set }V_1
CBV=f(\bar x^1)\text{ for a known feasible incumbent, or }CBV=-\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Each iteration either certifies infeasibility, returns a global optimum, or constructs }P_{k+1}=\bar P_k\setminus(x^k,b]\text{ and continues}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finiteness and Convergence of the Discrete Polyblock Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The all-discrete case has finite termination; the mixed case additionally requires uniform separation of the remaining coordinates from the lower box boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(s=n\), the discrete polyblock algorithm is finite. If \(s<n\) and there exists \(\alpha>0\) such that \[\min_{i=s+1,\ldots,n}(x_i-a_i)\ge\alpha\qquad\forall x\in H,\] then the algorithm either terminates finitely or generates an infinite sequence \(\{v^k\}\) converging to an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every coordinate is discrete, the discrete polyblock algorithm terminates finitely. In the mixed case, if every remaining coordinate of every point in H stays uniformly above its lower bound, the algorithm either terminates finitely or its selected vertices converge to an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s=n\Rightarrow\mathrm{DPA}\text{ is finite};\quad \left[s<n\text{ and the separation condition holds}\right]\Rightarrow\left(\mathrm{DPA}\text{ is finite or }v^k\to x^*\text{ for an optimal }x^*\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyblock vertex update after upper-orthant removal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric update used by polyblock outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq[a,b]\) be a polyblock with proper vertex set \(V\), and let \(x\in[a,b]\) satisfy \(V_*:=\{z\in V:x<z\}\neq\varnothing\). Then \(P':=P\setminus(x,b]\) is a polyblock with vertex set \[T'=(V\setminus V_*)\cup\{z^i=z+(x_i-z_i)e^i:z\in V_*,\ i=1,\ldots,n\}.\] Let \(V_*^+:=\{y\in V:x\leq y\}\). Its proper vertex set is obtained from \(T'\) by removing improper elements; for every \(z\in V_*\) and \(y\in V_*^+\), if \(J(z,y):=\{j:z_j>y_j\}=\{i\}\), then \(z^i\) is improper.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing the upper orthant above x from a polyblock replaces each proper vertex strictly above x by coordinate-cut candidates. The proper vertices are obtained by removing candidates identified as improper by the singleton-coordinate test.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq[a,b]\text{ is a polyblock with proper vertex set }V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P'=P\setminus(x,b]\text{ is a polyblock with vertex set }T',\quad J(z,y)=\{i\}\Rightarrow z^i\text{ is improper}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from a feasible incumbent \(x^0\in D\). At iteration \(k\), set \(\gamma_k=f(x^k)+\delta\) and invoke a complete global feasibility oracle for \(D_k=D\cap\{x:f(x)\ge\gamma_k\}\). If the oracle returns \(y^k\in D_k\), set \(x^{k+1}=y^k\) and repeat. If it certifies \(D_k=\varnothing\), stop and return \(x^k\). The empty-level certificate implies \(f(x)<f(x^k)+\delta\) for every \(x\in D\), so the returned incumbent is globally \(\delta\)-optimal in objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly seek a feasible point improving the incumbent by a fixed amount. Failure of a complete level-feasibility query certifies global objective accuracy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Successive Incumbent Transcending scheme for essential optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-problem iteration for the monotonic reformulation, with conditional essential-optimality and essential-infeasibility outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\eta>0\), set \(\gamma_0=f(b)\), and initialize \(\gamma\leftarrow\gamma_0\). Repeatedly solve \(Q_\gamma\). If \(\max(Q_\gamma)>0\), obtain an essential feasible point \(\widehat x\) satisfying \(f(\widehat x)\le\gamma\), set \(\gamma\leftarrow f(\widehat x)+\eta\), and repeat. If \(\max(Q_\gamma)\le0\), then no essential feasible point \(x\) satisfies \(f(x)\le\gamma\). If \(\gamma=f(\widehat x)+\eta\) for a previously found essential feasible point, return \(\widehat x\) as essential \(\eta\)-optimal; if \(\gamma=\gamma_0\), declare Q essentially infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize the cutoff at f(b) and repeatedly solve the cutoff master problem. A positive master optimum supplies an essential feasible incumbent and updates the cutoff to its value plus eta. A nonpositive optimum terminates: it certifies the previous incumbent as essential eta-optimal or, at the initial cutoff, declares essential infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \text{The master-problem implications used in Proposition 12.1 apply to each }Q_\gamma
Q_\gamma\text{ is solved globally at each iteration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max(Q_\gamma)\le0\Longrightarrow\begin{cases}\widehat x\text{ is essential }\eta\text{-optimal},&\gamma=f(\widehat x)+\eta,\\Q\text{ is essentially infeasible},&\gamma=\gamma_0.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinatewise γ-valid reduction of an SIT box
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit box-reduction construction for the target set referenced immediately before the extract; validity relies on Proposition 11.13 and that omitted antecedent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For $[p,q]\subset\mathbb R^n$, let $q^i=p+(q_i-p_i)e^i$, and for each indicated increasing function $\varphi:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$, let $N(\varphi)$ denote the largest $t\in[0,1]$ satisfying $\varphi(t)=0$. Then
$\operatorname{red}_\gamma[p,q]=\varnothing$ if $g(p)>0$ or $k_\gamma(q)<0$. If $g(p)\leq0$ and $k_\gamma(q)\geq0$, then $\operatorname{red}_\gamma[p,q]=[p',q']$, where
$q'=p+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(q_i-p_i)e^i$ and $p'=q'-\sum_{i=1}^n\beta_i(q_i'-p_i)e^i$,
with $\alpha_i=1$ when $g(q^i)\leq0$ and otherwise $\alpha_i=N(\varphi_i)$ for $\varphi_i(t)=g(p+t(q_i-p_i)e^i)$; similarly, $\beta_i=1$ when $k_\gamma(q'^{\,i})\geq0$ and otherwise $\beta_i=N(-\psi_i)$ for $\psi_i(t)=k_\gamma(q'-t(q_i'-p_i)e^i)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduction discards a box when its corner tests exclude the target set. Otherwise, it contracts the upper and lower coordinate bounds using the last zeros of the corresponding one-dimensional monotone functions.
assumptions_latex: \text{The target set referred to before the extract is fixed.}
\varphi_i\text{ and }-\psi_i\text{ have the monotonicity required for }N.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{red}_\gamma[p,q]=\begin{cases}\varnothing,&g(p)>0\text{ or }k_\gamma(q)<0,\\[p',q'],&g(p)\leq0\text{ and }k_\gamma(q)\geq0.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer incumbent-update scheme using the subprocedure $(SP_\gamma)$ at successively lower objective thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose $\varepsilon,
\eta>0$ and initialize $\gamma=\gamma_0:=f(a)-\eta$. Call $(SP_\gamma)$. Whenever it returns a nonisolated feasible point $\bar x$ with $f(\bar x)\leq\gamma$, reset $\gamma\leftarrow f(\bar x)-\eta$ and repeat. Otherwise stop. If $\gamma=f(\bar x)-\eta$ for a nonisolated feasible point $\bar x$, then $\bar x$ is essential $(\varepsilon,\eta)$-optimal; if $\gamma=
\gamma_0$, then $(P)$ has no $\varepsilon$-essential feasible solution. If $f(D)$ is compact, the scheme is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scheme repeatedly seeks a nonisolated feasible point below the current objective threshold and then lowers that threshold by eta. Failure after an update certifies essential approximate optimality, while failure at the initial threshold certifies epsilon-essential infeasibility. Compactness of the feasible objective image and positive eta ensure finite termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The scheme terminates after finitely many updates and yields either an essential }(\varepsilon,\eta)\text{-optimal nonisolated feasible point or the conclusion that no }\varepsilon\text{-essential feasible solution exists.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose $\varepsilon,\eta>0$, set $\gamma_0=f(a)-\eta$, $\mathcal P_1=\{[a,b]\}$, $\mathcal R_1=\varnothing$, $\gamma=\gamma_0$, and $k=1$. Reduce each $M\in\mathcal P_k$ to a subbox preserving $\min\{g(x)\mid f(x)\leq\gamma,
 x\in M\}$, compute a lower bound $\beta(M)$ for $g$ over the relevant points, require $\beta(M)<+\infty\Rightarrow\{x\in M\mid f(x)\leq\gamma\}\neq\varnothing$, and delete boxes satisfying $\beta(M)>-\varepsilon$. Add surviving boxes to the reserve. If the reserve is empty, terminate with $\varepsilon$-essential infeasibility when $\gamma=\gamma_0$, or with essential $(\varepsilon,\eta)$-optimality of the current nonisolated incumbent $\bar x$ when $\gamma=f(\bar x)-\eta$. Otherwise select $M_k$ minimizing $\beta$, and choose $x^k,y^k\in M_k$ satisfying $f(x^k)\leq\gamma$ and $g(y^k)-\beta(M_k)=o(\lVert x^k-y^k\rVert)$. If $g(x^k)<-\varepsilon$, treat $x^k$ as a nonisolated feasible solution and initialize or improve $\bar x$ as specified. Bisect $M_k$ at $v^k=(x^k+y^k)/2$ along an index $j_k\in\arg\max_j|y_j^k-x_j^k|$, replace it by the two subboxes, increment $k$, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm reduces and bounds boxes, prunes boxes whose bounds exclude epsilon-essential feasibility, and terminates with an infeasibility or approximate-optimality certificate when no boxes remain. Otherwise it selects the lowest-bound box, tests paired points, handles any strictly margin-feasible incumbent, and adaptively bisects along the largest coordinate discrepancy.
assumptions_latex: \beta(M)\text{ is a lower bound of the prescribed kind}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Each iteration either terminates with the stated essential-infeasibility or essential-optimality conclusion, or continues after incumbent handling and adaptive bisection.}

knowledge_statements.title: Difference-of-Convex Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional DC representation of an objective and finitely many inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\). A DC program has the form \(\min_{x\in X}\{g_0(x)-h_0(x):g_i(x)-h_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Introducing \(t\in\mathbb R\) gives the epigraph formulation \[\min_{x\in X,\,t\in\mathbb R} t-h_0(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_0(x)\leq t,\quad g_i(x)-h_i(x)\leq0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] For every feasible \(x\) of the original problem, choosing \(t=g_0(x)\) gives the same objective value, while every feasible \((x,t)\) of the epigraph problem satisfies \(t-h_0(x)\geq g_0(x)-h_0(x)\). Hence the two problems have the same infimum, and whenever an optimum is attained their optimal \(x\)-components coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Express the objective and each inequality as a difference of two convex functions. An epigraph variable for the positive convex objective component produces a formulation with the same optimal value and the same optimal x-components when optima exist.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i,h_i:X\to\mathbb R\) are finite-valued convex functions for \(i=0,1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and epigraph formulations have the same infimum; when an optimum is attained, their minimizing \(x\)-components coincide.

notation.meaning: convex components of inequality constraint i
epigraph variable for the positive convex objective component

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrarily Weak and Inconsistent Equivalent DC Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition-dependent relaxation failure on fixed and shrinking intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f\equiv0\) on \(B=[-r,r]\), write \(f(x)=Mx^2-Mx^2\). The endpoint secant majorant of \(h(x)=Mx^2\) is \(a_B(x)=Mr^2\), so \(\underline f_B(x)=Mx^2-Mr^2\) and \(\min_B f-\min_B\underline f_B=Mr^2\). On the fixed interval \(r=1\), this gap is arbitrarily large as \(M\to\infty\). On shrinking intervals, choosing \(M=r^{-2}\) keeps the gap equal to one even as \(r\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent DC decompositions can make a bound arbitrarily weak, and changing the decomposition with the cell can prevent consistency even on shrinking cells.
assumptions_latex: The subtracted convex quadratic is replaced by its endpoint secant majorant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_B f-\min_B\underline f_B=Mr^2;\quad M=r^{-2}\Longrightarrow\text{gap}=1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restriction Monotonicity with a Fixed DC Lower Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength improvement under spatial restriction when the lower model is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(B'\subseteq B\) and the same valid lower model \(\underline f_B\leq f\) is used on both cells, then \[\inf_{x\in B'}\underline f_B(x)\geq\inf_{x\in B}\underline f_B(x).\] Hence domain restriction cannot weaken a fixed relaxation; parent-child bound monotonicity may fail only when the model, its decomposition, or its parameters are changed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking a cell strengthens a fixed lower model, whereas rebuilding the model can reverse bound monotonicity.
assumptions_latex: \(\underline f_B\) is a valid lower model on \(B\) and is reused on \(B'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{B'}\underline f_B\geq\inf_B\underline f_B.

assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a compact convex cell with diameter \(d(B)\).
\(f=g-h\) on \(B\), with \(g\) convex and \(h\) convex and Lipschitz with constant \(M_B\).
\(\ell_B\) is an affine minorant of \(-h\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation error is bounded by \(0\leq f(x)-\underline f_B(x)\leq2M_Bd(B)\) for every \(x\in B\), so diameter reduction forces consistency, whereas nonshrinking cells need not yield exact bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\ell_B(x)\leq-h(x)\) on \(B\) and that \(\ell_B\) touches \(-h\) at some \(z_B\in B\). Then \(\underline f_B=g+\ell_B\) is convex and satisfies \(\underline f_B\leq f\) on \(B\). Since both \(h\) and the touching affine support have slopes bounded in norm by \(M_B\), \[0\leq f(x)-\underline f_B(x)\leq2M_Bd(B),\qquad x\in B.\] Thus nested cells with \(d(B_k)\to0\) have vanishing relaxation error. Without shrinking diameters or uniform local slope control, the relaxation gap may remain positive, so pruning based on asymptotic exactness is unjustified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DC lower bounds become exact on shrinking cells under local Lipschitz control; without shrinking or slope control, a persistent relaxation gap can defeat global certification.

children.title: Generalized-Descent Search
children.top_down_role: Search families extending descent concepts beyond ordinary local improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Descent Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized descent alternating value-nonincreasing local minimization with attempts at strict interbasin escape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(y_0\in X\), set \(x_0=\mathcal L(y_0)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), call \(\mathcal E(x_k)\). If it returns \(y_k\in X\) with \(f(y_k)<f(x_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=\mathcal L(y_k)\); then \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(y_k)<f(x_k)\). If it certifies that \(\{z\in X:f(z)<f(x_k)\}=\varnothing\), stop and output \(x_k\) as a global minimizer. If it fails without that certificate, stop or continue according to the prescribed search policy, but regard \(x_k\) only as an uncertified incumbent. Thus generalized descent requires strict improvement between accepted local minima, while global optimality requires a complete escape certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized descent alternates value-nonincreasing local optimization with attempts to enter a strictly better basin. Failure establishes global optimality only when the escape procedure certifies that no lower-valued feasible point exists.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
The local minimization operator \(\mathcal L:X\to X\) returns a local minimizer and satisfies \(f(\mathcal L(y))\leq f(y)\) for every \(y\in X\).

At a local minimizer \(x\), the escape operator \(\mathcal E\) returns either a point \(y\in X\) with \(f(y)<f(x)\), a valid certificate that no such point exists, or an explicitly uncertified failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every successful outer iteration strictly decreases the accepted local-minimum value; global optimality follows only from a valid certificate that no point in \(X\) has value below the incumbent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Descent over Finitely Many Local-Minimum Levels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successful-transition bound when generalized descent can accept only finitely many distinct local-minimum objective levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{f(x):x\text{ is an eligible local minimizer}\}\) have \(m<\infty\) distinct values. If each successful generalized-descent transition accepts \(x_{k+1}\) only when \(f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)\), then any run contains at most \(m-1\) successful transitions. This bound does not imply that an unsuccessful escape attempt is a global-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With only m eligible local-minimum levels, strict generalized descent can make at most m minus one successful transitions; an ensuing failed escape is still uncertified unless it excludes every lower-valued feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(V=\{f(x):x\text{ is an eligible local minimizer}\}\) has \(m<\infty\) distinct values.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized descent adapts local minimization to global optimization either by modifying the equation governing a local-descent trajectory or by repeatedly applying a local algorithm to objectives modified to exclude previously found local minima. These approaches are called trajectory methods and penalty methods, respectively.

children.title: Local-to-Global Transitions
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms governing movement from local improvement into broader exploration.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in X\) is a local minimizer returned by a local solver.
The escape test is complete for the strict sublevel set below \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transition from local to global status occurs exactly when the strict lower sublevel set is empty: \(S_x=\varnothing\iff x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in X}f(z)\).

notation.meaning: strict sublevel set below the current local-minimum value

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S_x=\{z\in X:f(z)<f(x)\}\). Then \[x\in X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in X}f(z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S_x=\varnothing.\] Hence an escape procedure converts the local conclusion at \(x\) into a global conclusion precisely when it searches \(S_x\) completely and certifies emptiness. More generally, if it certifies \(f(z)\geq f(x)-\varepsilon\) for every \(z\in X\), then \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-global, meaning \(f(x)\leq\min_{z\in X}f(z)+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local minimizer becomes globally certified exactly when no feasible point has lower value; excluding values more than epsilon lower yields epsilon-global certification.

children.title: Trajectory Stagnation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Path structures that trap or stall trajectory-based global search.

assumptions_latex: The trajectory rule generates trial points only in a subset \(R\subseteq X\).
A better basin contains a nonempty relatively open set \(V\subseteq X\setminus\overline R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No generated trajectory point enters \(V\); therefore a local solver launched only from the trajectory cannot discover the better minimizer in that basin.

notation.meaning: reachable set of the trajectory rule
unreached portion of an improving attraction basin

source_refs.locator: 3. Methods of Generalized Descent p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every trial point generated from the incumbent \(x^c\) lie in \(R\), and suppose \(V\subseteq X\setminus\overline R\) lies in the attraction basin of a local minimizer \(x^b\) with \(f(x^b)<f(x^c)\). Then no trajectory launch belongs to \(V\), so repeated local searches restricted to those launches cannot reach \(x^b\) through \(V\). Stagnation may therefore occur even when objective values along the generated path decrease locally. A global convergence claim requires a reachability, density, exhaustive-restart, or valid lower-bound condition that rules out such hidden improving basins.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trajectory stagnates globally when its reachable set misses an open part of every route into a better basin, even if it continues making local progress.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Missing one relatively open subset V of an attraction basin does not prevent other reachable launches from entering the same basin and finding its minimizer. A valid failure result needs the whole relevant launch region or every route into the improving basin to be unreachable, with a direct supporting locator.

children.title: Homotopy Global Methods
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for parameterized continuation approaches to global search.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A regular continuation path can be followed to a zero of \(H(\cdot,1)\), but global optimization additionally requires an endpoint-selection or exhaustive-path condition linking terminal zeros to global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic regular continuation scheme; the intended global-selection mechanism remains source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((x_0,\lambda_0)=(x_0,0)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), predict a point on the solution manifold \(H(x,\lambda)=0\) using a tangent satisfying \(D_xH\,\dot x+D_\lambda H\,\dot\lambda=0\), then correct it by solving \(H(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=0\). Adapt the step size and continue until \(\lambda_{k+1}=1\). If \(D_xH(x(\lambda),\lambda)\) is nonsingular along the path, local continuation is well-defined. Output a terminal point only after applying the method's prescribed rule for selecting globally minimizing endpoints or exhausting all relevant paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homotopy methods track solutions from an easy parameter value to the target problem; regular tracking alone does not ensure that the selected endpoint is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Homotopy Global Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This immutable node is a topic-level navigation container, not an exact algorithm leaf. The generic predictor-corrector continuation algorithm therefore does not fit the container, and no source identifies a specific global homotopy method or endpoint-selection guarantee.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary labelling induced by the maximal component residual, with smallest-index tie breaking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(i=\min\{j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}: f_j(x)-x_j=\max_{1\leq k\leq n}(f_k(x)-x_k)\}\). Define \(\ell(x)=1\) if \(f_i(x)-x_i\geq0\), and \(\ell(x)=0\) if \(f_i(x)-x_i<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the smallest index attaining the largest residual f_j(x)-x_j. Label x by 1 if that residual is nonnegative and by 0 otherwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell(x)=\begin{cases}1,&f_i(x)-x_i\geq0,\\0,&f_i(x)-x_i<0.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-started continuation for finding a fixed point of a smooth map from the closure of a compact convex domain into its interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be bounded, open, and convex, let \(\overline D\) be compact, and suppose \(\partial D\) consists of finitely many smooth hypersurfaces. Let \(f:\overline D\to D\) have continuous first and second derivatives, and set \(C=\{x\in\overline D:f(x)=x\}\). For \(x\notin C\), let \(H(x)\) be the point where the ray from \(f(x)\) through \(x\) meets \(\partial D\). Starting from a regular point \(x^0\in\partial D\), follow the component of \(H^{-1}(x^0)\) containing \(x^0\). Along this component, where \(\operatorname{rank}H'(x)=n-1\), select \(z(x)\ne0\) with \(H'(x)z(x)=0\) and track \(x'(t)=z(x(t))\), \(x(0)=x^0\). The continuation curve satisfies \(H(x(t))=x^0\), cannot meet \(\partial D\) at a point other than \(x^0\), and contains a fixed point of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct the radial boundary map associated with f and, from a regular boundary point, track the corresponding level-set component using a null direction of its derivative. Under the stated smoothness and rank conditions, this continuation curve cannot return to another boundary point and contains a fixed point of f.

\partial D\text{ consists of finitely many smooth hypersurfaces}

x^0\in\partial D\text{ is regular for the followed level set}

children.title: Local-Minimum Escape Transformations
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for transformations designed to escape known local minima.

children.title: Tunneling Transformations
children.top_down_role: Landscape transformations designed to move search beyond a known local minimizer.

assumptions_latex: The transformed search excludes \(x^c\) and points where \(f(x)=f(x^c)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every negative value of \(T_p\) identifies a point strictly better than \(x^c\); thus minimizing the transform can provide an escape from the incumbent level set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pole-based tunneling transform for detecting points below an incumbent local-minimum level.

source_refs.locator: 3. Methods of Generalized Descent p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X\setminus\{x^c\}\) with \(f(x)\neq f(x^c)\), define \[T_p(x;x^c)=\frac{f(x)-f(x^c)}{\lVert x-x^c\rVert^p}.\] Because the denominator is positive, \(T_p(x;x^c)<0\) if and only if \(f(x)<f(x^c)\). Consequently, any feasible point with negative transformed value is a directly verifiable escape point. The pole at \(x^c\) discourages return to the incumbent, while the transformation preserves the sign of improvement; it does not by itself guarantee that a local minimization of \(T_p\) will find a negative value when one exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pole-based transform has negative value exactly at points better than the current local minimizer, so finding a negative transformed value certifies an escape.
knowledge_statements.title: Tunneling Transformations

source_witnesses.locator: 3. Methods of Generalized Descent p. 53

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sign equivalence of the displayed quotient is elementary, but calling the singularity a pole that discourages return is not valid for every p>0; its limiting behavior depends on p and the local growth of f. The specific tunneling transformation and admissible exponent require direct source confirmation.

children.title: Filled-Function Transformations
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-landscape families designed to suppress attraction to known local minima.

assumptions_latex: \(x^c\) is a nonglobal local minimizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local minimization of a filled function cannot terminate at a nonincumbent point in the old basin and, when it reaches a point below the incumbent level, supplies an escape start for minimizing \(f\).

notation.meaning: attraction basin of the incumbent under the fixed local solver
filled function based at the incumbent
strict lower sublevel set of the incumbent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational filled-function definition relative to a fixed local solver and incumbent basin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B(x^c)\) be the attraction basin of \(x^c\) for a fixed local solver and let \(S_{x^c}=\{x\in X:f(x)<f(x^c)\}\). A function \(P(\cdot;x^c):X\to\mathbb{R}\) is a filled function at \(x^c\) if \(x^c\) is a strict local maximizer of \(P\), \(P\) has no local minimizer in \(B(x^c)\setminus\{x^c\}\), and every local minimizer of \(P\) reachable from a descent launch outside the incumbent satisfies or leads to \(S_{x^c}\). The transformation fills the incumbent basin while preserving an avenue toward a strictly lower objective level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filled function turns the current minimizer into a local maximum, removes competing minima from its basin, and directs transformed descent toward a lower objective level.
knowledge_statements.title: Filled-Function Transformations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Filled-function definitions impose source-dependent properties, and the clause that every reachable local minimizer 'satisfies or leads to' the lower sublevel set is not mathematically defined. A direct definition or theorem locator is required.

children.title: Escape-Basin Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural choices governing which neighboring basins become reachable.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and partitioned into attraction basins for a fixed deterministic local solver.
A finite candidate set \(Y_k\subset X\) and valid basin lower estimates are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Discarding only basins whose valid lower estimate is at least \(f(x^c)\) preserves every improving basin; fair selection among the remaining candidates eventually launches in each represented improving basin.

notation.meaning: finite candidate launch set at iteration k
estimated or identified basin containing y
valid lower estimate for a basin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair basin selection using valid lower estimates and transformed candidate launches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), remove every \(y\in Y_k\) whose basin is already explored or satisfies \(L(B(y))\geq f(x^c)\). From the remaining candidates select \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y_k}L(B(y)),\] breaking ties by a fair rule. Apply the local solver at \(y_k\); if it returns \(x^{\mathrm{new}}\) with \(f(x^{\mathrm{new}})<f(x^c)\), replace the incumbent. Mark \(B(y_k)\) explored and augment \(Y_k\) using the prescribed escape transformation. Stop globally only when every unvisited basin has a valid lower estimate at least \(f(x^c)\); otherwise return an uncertified incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select an unexplored basin with the best valid lower estimate, launch local search there, and certify globality only after all remaining basin bounds exceed the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Escape-Basin Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed algorithm assumes identifiable attraction basins and valid lower bounds for each basin, neither of which is defined or sourced. Its fairness and eventual-coverage conclusion also requires a precise rule governing candidate-set augmentation and basin representation.

children.title: Transformation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where transformed landscapes fail to reveal useful escape directions.

assumptions_latex: A local escape transformation is searched only inside a neighborhood contained in the attraction basin of the right-hand local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformation may certify no local escape while the left-hand local minimizer has strictly smaller objective value; hence incomplete transformed search cannot certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete double-well failure caused by restricting transformed search to the incumbent basin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), the tilted double-well function \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2+\delta x\) has two strict local minimizers \(x_L<0<x_R\), with \(f(x_L)<f(x_R)\). Let a tunneling or filled-function subproblem be solved only on a closed neighborhood \(N_R\) contained in the attraction basin of \(x_R\) and disjoint from the strict sublevel set \(\{x:f(x)<f(x_R)\}\). Then no transformed trial restricted to \(N_R\) can reveal \(x_L\), although \(x_R\) is nonglobal. Failure of this restricted transformation therefore supplies no global certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tilted double well defeats an escape transformation confined to the worse well: local failure to escape does not exclude a better minimum elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tilted double well does exhibit two unequal local minima for a suitable explicit range of delta, but that range is not stated and the claimed behavior is not tied to a defined tunneling or filled-function transformation. A direct source or a transformation-specific formulation is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic iterative random search with history-dependent batch sizes and joint sampling distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(n_1\ge1\) and a probability distribution \(P_1\) on \(A^{n_1}\), and set \(j=1\). At iteration \(j\), jointly sample \((x_1^{(j)},\ldots,x_{n_j}^{(j)})\sim P_j\) and evaluate \(f\) at all sampled points. Test the stopping criterion and terminate if it holds. Otherwise, use all sampled points and objective values from iterations \(1,\ldots,j\) to choose an integer \(n_{j+1}\ge1\) and construct a probability distribution \(P_{j+1}\) on \(A^{n_{j+1}}\); replace \(j\) by \(j+1\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, jointly draw and evaluate a batch of feasible points. Unless the stopping criterion holds, use the complete search history to choose the next batch size and joint sampling distribution, then repeat.

n_{j+1}\in\mathbb N,\quad n_{j+1}\ge1,\quad P_{j+1}\text{ may depend on all observations through iteration }j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure generates adaptive random-search batches until the stopping criterion holds.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the adaptive random sampling and stopping structure of global random search; the listed convergence modes are possible forms of analysis, not automatic guarantees.

For $j\ge 2$, $P_j$ may depend on $x_1,\ldots,x_{j-1}$ and on their possibly noisy objective-function evaluations. Later sampling distributions may adapt to earlier points and possibly noisy evaluations, and stopping may be deterministic or random and data-dependent. Depending on the algorithm and assumptions, convergence results may be almost sure, in probability, or confidence-qualified; convergence is not guaranteed merely by this definition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample performance of independent pure random search for a fixed near-optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_\varepsilon=\{x:f(x)<f^*+\varepsilon\}\) have sampling probability \(p_\varepsilon=\mu(A_\varepsilon)\). For \(n\) independent draws, \[\Pr\!\left(\min_{1\le i\le n}f(X_i)<f^*+\varepsilon\right)=1-(1-p_\varepsilon)^n.\] If \(0<p_\varepsilon<1\), confidence at least \(1-\alpha\) is attained exactly when \((1-p_\varepsilon)^n\le\alpha\), equivalently \[n\ge\left\lceil\frac{\log\alpha}{\log(1-p_\varepsilon)}\right\rceil.\] The first hitting time has mean \(1/p_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure random search hits an epsilon-optimal set with probability one minus the corresponding miss probability; expected waiting time is the reciprocal of its sampling mass.
assumptions_latex: \(0<p_\varepsilon<1\) for the displayed finite-count and mean formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(U_n<f^*+\varepsilon)=1-(1-p_\varepsilon)^n,\qquad \mathbb E[\tau_\varepsilon]=p_\varepsilon^{-1}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pure random search on a finite product space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform random sampling with incumbent retention for simulation-based maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathcal X=\prod_{i=1}^N\mathcal A(i)$, where every $\mathcal A(i)$ is finite, and let $p(i,a)=1/|\mathcal A(i)|$. In every iteration, sample $x\in\mathcal X$ uniformly by selecting its coordinates according to these probabilities, evaluate $f(x)$ by simulation, and replace $(x_{\mathrm{best}},R_{\mathrm{best}})$ by $(x,f(x))$ whenever $f(x)>R_{\mathrm{best}}$. Initialize $R_{\mathrm{best}}$ below every possible objective value and stop according to the prescribed iteration-counter rule.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{\mathrm{best}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}\{f(x^{(m)}):x^{(m)}\text{ was sampled during the run}\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q^*>0\) be the probability of selecting the global optimum under pure random search, and let \(M\) be the number of iterations required to select it for the first time. Otherwise, draw \(Y_{n+1}\) from the probability measure \(\lambda(\cdot\cap R_n)/\lambda(R_n)\). Under the stated positive-measure condition on every near-optimal set, the incumbent values converge almost surely to \(f^\star\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates idealized PAS iterations from implementable evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: PAS presumes exact sampling from \(\lambda(\cdot\cap R_n)/\lambda(R_n)\). If this is implemented by independent uniform proposals on \(X\) rejected outside \(R_n\), the expected proposals for one accepted update equal \(\lambda(X)/\lambda(R_n)\), which can diverge near the optimum. Logarithmic accepted-iteration bounds therefore do not imply logarithmic evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PAS's idealized rate assumes an exact improving-region sampler; rejection implementations may have reciprocal-volume evaluation cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pure Adaptive Search and Its Weak Variant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional sampling from strict or non-strict improving sublevel sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $x_1\sim P$ on $A$. For $j\geq1$, define
\[
y_{oj}=\min_{1\leq i\leq j}f(x_i),\qquad S_j=\{x\in A:f(x)<y_{oj}\}.
\]
Whenever $P(S_j)>0$, pure adaptive search draws $x_{j+1}$ from the conditional distribution
\[
P_{j+1}(U)=\frac{P(U\cap S_j)}{P(S_j)}
\]
for every Borel set $U\subseteq A$. Thus each new point is a strict record, and the generated points are dependent in general. If $P$ is uniform on $A$, the conditional distribution is uniform on $S_j$. Weak pure adaptive search instead samples using the non-strict sublevel set $W_{x_j}=\{x\in A:f(x)\leq f(x_j)\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure adaptive search samples each next point from the original distribution conditioned on strictly improving the current record. Each accepted sample is therefore a new record, and the samples are generally dependent. The weak variant uses the corresponding non-strict sublevel set.
assumptions_latex: P(S_j)>0\text{ whenever the conditional step is executed}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{j+1}(U)=\frac{P(U\cap S_j)}{P(S_j)},\quad S_j=\{x\in A:f(x)<y_{oj}\};\qquad W_{x_j}=\{x\in A:f(x)\leq f(x_j)\}\text{ for the weak variant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequence-driven covering search with unequal adaptive balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluates a prescribed point sequence while skipping covered candidates and adapting radii through the kth order statistic of accepted objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $k\geq1$, first evaluate $z_1,\ldots,z_k$ from $Z_\infty=(z_i)_{i\geq1}$, set $x_l=z_l$ and $\varepsilon_l=\delta/L$ for $l=1,\ldots,k$, and let $y^*_{k,k}=\max_{1\leq l\leq k}f(x_l)$. For each subsequent $z_{i+1}$, skip it if $\rho(z_{i+1},x_l)\leq\varepsilon_l$ for some accepted point. Otherwise accept it as $x_j$ and evaluate $f(x_j)$. If $f(x_j)\geq y^*_{k,j-1}$, keep $y^*_{k,j}=y^*_{k,j-1}$ and set $\varepsilon_j=(f(x_j)-y^*_{k,j}+\delta)/L$. If $f(x_j)<y^*_{k,j-1}$, redefine $y^*_{k,j}$ as the kth smallest value among $f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_j)$ and reset $\varepsilon_l=\delta/L+\max\{0,f(x_l)-y^*_{k,j}\}/L$ for every $l=1,\ldots,j$. Continue until the stopping condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the first k points of a prescribed sequence. Skip later candidates lying in an existing exclusion ball and evaluate uncovered candidates. Radii depend on the current kth-smallest accepted value and are all recomputed whenever that order statistic decreases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(z_{i+1},x_l)\leq\varepsilon_l\text{ for some }l\implies z_{i+1}\text{ is skipped},\qquad \varepsilon_l=\frac{\delta+\max\{0,f(x_l)-y^*_{k,j}\}}{L}\text{ after recomputation}.

children.title: Stratified Random Search
children.top_down_role: Random search organized through a partitioned sampling domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise finite-design guarantee once every stratum is represented.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\) exactly partition \(X\), choose \(x_j\in S_j\), and set \(\delta=\max_j\operatorname{diam}(S_j)\). For an objective with modulus of continuity \(\omega_f\), \[0\le\min_jf(x_j)-f^\star\le\omega_f(\delta).\] For an \(L\)-Lipschitz objective the bound is \(L\delta\), independently of how representatives were randomized within their strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One representative from every exact stratum gives an error bounded by the objective's modulus of continuity at the largest stratum diameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_jf(x_j)-f^\star\le\omega_f(\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stratum-Diameter Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a genuine covering partition and fixes boundary allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite stratification of compact metric space \(X\) is a family of nonempty measurable sets \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\) satisfying \(X=\bigcup_jS_j\) and \(S_i\cap S_j=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\), with boundaries assigned explicitly. A one-per-stratum design chooses \(x_j\in S_j\); a randomized design draws \(X_j\) from a distribution supported on \(S_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stratified design exactly partitions the entire domain and selects or samples at least one representative from every stratum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every point, including boundary points, belongs to a represented stratum.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Stratified Design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for worst-case continuous-objective coverage claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partition only up to reference-measure zero need not cover every possible minimizer. If an omitted point is positively separated from all represented sets, a continuous objective can have its unique minimum there while sampled values remain separated from the optimum. Even for an exact partition, the diameter certificate fails if a stratum receives no representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting a separated null-set point or leaving a stratum unrepresented can destroy worst-case optimization coverage.
assumptions_latex: A point is omitted and positively separated from represented sets, or some exact stratum has no representative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency for every continuous objective and the diameter certificate need not hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Omitted-Set and Unrepresented-Stratum Failures

assumptions_latex: The compact region \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is partitioned into measurable strata \(S_{n,1},\ldots,S_{n,m_n}\).
Each stratum has positive reference measure and its conditional sampling distribution has support equal to that stratum.
The maximal stratum diameter tends to zero as the total number of evaluations grows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every continuous \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), the best sampled value converges almost surely to \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One conditionally independent draw per shrinking measurable stratum, with best-so-far output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(n\), construct a partition \(X=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m_n}S_{n,j}\) up to null sets. Independently for each \(j\), draw \(X_{n,j}\) from the reference measure conditioned on \(S_{n,j}\), evaluate \(f(X_{n,j})\), and return the best point among all samples generated through stage \(n\). If \(\delta_n=\max_j\operatorname{diam}(S_{n,j})\to0\), then every point of \(X\) lies arbitrarily close to a sampled stratum representative. Uniform continuity of \(f\) on compact \(X\) consequently yields convergence of the best sampled value to the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the domain into increasingly fine strata, sample once within each stratum, and retain the best evaluation; shrinking strata ensure consistency for continuous objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Stratified Random Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. Moreover, a partition only up to null sets need not cover a minimizer located in an omitted null set, so the stated assumptions do not establish the claimed consistency for every continuous objective. The statement also contains proof text. The algorithm kind otherwise fits the leaf.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proper allocation characterizes stochastic dominance of stratified sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes proportional allocation as sufficient for stochastic dominance over independent sampling and gives a witness showing that any nonproportional allocation destroys uniform dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathcal R_k$ be a fixed partition of $A$ into $k\leq n$ subsets, let $\mathcal F=C^p(A)$ for some $0\leq p\leq\infty$, and let $\mathcal P_{k,L}$ be the stratified procedure with $l_i\geq0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^k l_i=n$. If $l_i=nq_i$ for every $i$, where $q_i=P(A_i)$, then $\mathcal P_{k,L}$ stochastically dominates the independent procedure $\mathcal P_1$ on $\mathcal F$ under criterion (3.43). If $l_i\neq nq_i$ for at least one $i$, then $\mathcal P_{k,L}$ does not stochastically dominate $\mathcal P_1$; moreover, there exist $f^*\in\mathcal F$ and $t$ such that $F_{k,L}(f^*,t)<F_1(f^*,t)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed partition and sample budget, allocating samples in exact proportion to stratum probability makes stratified random search stochastically dominate independent sampling over the stated function class. If any allocation is nonproportional, uniform dominance fails, and a function and threshold witness the adverse cdf inequality.
assumptions_latex: $\mathcal R_k$ is a fixed partition of $A$ into $k\leq n$ subsets.
$F_{k,L}(f,t)$ and $F_1(f,t)$ are the record-value c.d.f.s specified by criterion (3.43).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic moment ratio for stratified and independent random search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives an almost-sure asymptotic ratio of positive record-error moments as the number of strata grows while the sample count per stratum remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that $P$ and the class $\mathcal F_*$ of continuous functions $f(x)=\varphi(x-x_*)$ having a unique global minimizer $x_*(f)$ satisfy condition (2.42) for $F=F_f$ with some $\alpha>0$. Suppose $x_*$ has distribution $R$ on $A$, where $R$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure. If $n=kl$, $l$ is fixed, and $k\to\infty$, then for every $p>0$, with $R$-probability one, $$\frac{\mathbb E\left(f_*[X_{k,l}]-m\right)^p}{\mathbb E\left(f_*[X_{1,n}]-m\right)^p}=l^{p/\alpha}\frac{\Gamma(l+1)}{\Gamma(p/\alpha+l+1)}+o(1),\qquad n\to\infty.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under condition (2.42) and the stated distributional assumption on the unique minimizer, keeping l samples per stratum while increasing the number of strata makes the ratio of stratified to independent record-error moments converge almost surely to an explicit gamma-function expression.
assumptions_latex: $f\in\mathcal F_*$ is continuous, has the form $f(x)=\varphi(x-x_*)$, and has a unique global minimizer $x_*$.
$x_*\sim R$, and $R$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on $A$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\mathbb E\left(f_*[X_{k,l}]-m\right)^p}{\mathbb E\left(f_*[X_{1,n}]-m\right)^p}=l^{p/\alpha}\frac{\Gamma(l+1)}{\Gamma(p/\alpha+l+1)}+o(1)\quad(n\to\infty),\qquad R\text{-a.s.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines conditional sampling on a measurable partition, proportional allocation, the product sampling law, and independent sampling as the one-stratum case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $P$ be a probability measure on $A$, and let $A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A_i$ be a partition into pairwise disjoint connected measurable sets with $q_i=P(A_i)>0$. Define $P_i(B)=P(B\cap A_i)/q_i$ for measurable $B\subseteq A$. Given integers $l_i\geq0$ with $\sum_{i=1}^k l_i=n$, a stratified sample is $X_{k,L}=(x_{i,j})$, where the variables are mutually independent and $x_{i,j}\sim P_i$ for $1\leq j\leq l_i$. Its joint law is $Q_{k,L}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^k P_i^{\otimes l_i}$. It is proper if $l_i=nq_i$ for every $i$. For $k=1$, the construction is independent sampling from $P$. For an objective $f$, $f_*[X]=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\geq m:=\min_{x\in A}f(x)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stratified sample draws mutually independent points from the conditional distribution within each positive-probability stratum. It is proper when the number assigned to each stratum is proportional to its probability mass. With one stratum the construction becomes ordinary independent sampling from P, and the best sampled value cannot be below the global minimum.
assumptions_latex: $A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A_i$, with the $A_i$ connected, measurable, pairwise disjoint, and $P(A_i)=q_i>0$.
The variables $x_{i,j}$ are mutually independent and satisfy $x_{i,j}\sim P_i$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_{k,L}=\bigotimes_{i=1}^kP_i^{\otimes l_i},\qquad \operatorname{proper}(X_{k,L})\iff(\forall i)\ l_i=nq_i,\qquad k=1\Rightarrow Q_{1,n}=P^{\otimes n},\qquad f_*[X]\geq m.

children.title: Quasirandom Search
children.top_down_role: Global exploration based on low-discrepancy sampling designs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts declared fill-distance or star-discrepancy rates into objective error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a design prefix has fill distance \(h_n\le Ca_n\), then for modulus of continuity \(\omega_f\), \[0\le\min_{i\le n}f(u_i)-f^\star\le\omega_f(Ca_n).\] On \([0,1]^d\), the bound \(h_n\le2(D_n^*)^{1/d}\) gives error at most \(\omega_f(2(D_n^*)^{1/d})\). For an \(L\)-Hölder objective of exponent \(\alpha\), this is at most \(L2^\alpha(D_n^*)^{\alpha/d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasirandom prefix's covering or discrepancy rate converts through the objective's modulus of continuity into a deterministic optimization-error rate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuous on the compact unit cube.
The stated fill-distance or discrepancy bound holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_n-f^\star\le\omega_f(h_n)\le\omega_f(2(D_n^*)^{1/d})\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard quantitative design class for quasirandom search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((u_i)_{i\ge1}\subset[0,1]^d\) is low discrepancy with respect to anchored boxes when its prefix star discrepancies satisfy \(D_n^*=O(n^{-1}(\log n)^d)\). More generally, \(D_n^*\to0\) is equivalent to uniform distribution of the sequence on the unit cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low-discrepancy sequences have rapidly vanishing anchored-box discrepancy; vanishing star discrepancy characterizes uniform distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(D_n^*\) is the star discrepancy of the first \(n\) points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Low discrepancy implies \(D_n^*\to0\) and uniform distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Discrepancy Sequence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits conclusions drawn merely from labeling a design randomized or low discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Random shifting or scrambling supports pathwise optimization convergence only when the selected construction preserves a deterministic or almost-sure vanishing-discrepancy or vanishing-covering guarantee. Randomization alone supplies no such guarantee. Likewise, discrepancy affects pointwise optimization only through a valid discrepancy-to-covering conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomization alone does not ensure coverage, and discrepancy must be converted geometrically before it bounds optimization error.
assumptions_latex: Only randomization or an unquantified discrepancy label is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No pathwise optimization-error guarantee follows without a construction-specific coverage implication.
knowledge_statements.title: Construction-Specific Randomization Boundary

assumptions_latex: The deterministic or randomized point sequence has covering radius tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent values satisfy \(\min_{1\le i\le n}f(U_i)\to\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Covering radius in the chosen norm
Best objective value through evaluation n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic low-dispersion sequences or randomized variants used as global-search evaluation sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select a space-filling sequence \((U_i)_{i\ge1}\subset[0,1]^d\), such as a low-discrepancy sequence, optionally after a random digital shift or scrambling that preserves its coverage order. Evaluate \(f(U_n)\) sequentially and output an index \(i_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le n}f(U_i)\). If its covering radius \(h_n\to0\), then for a minimizer \(x^\star\) there is a sampled point within distance \(h_n\) of \(x^\star\). Hence continuity gives \(f(U_{i_n})\to f(x^\star)\). Randomization changes the sampling law but not this conclusion whenever \(h_n\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a space-filling low-discrepancy sequence and retain its best point; vanishing covering radius guarantees convergence for continuous objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Van der Corput and Halton Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the radical-inverse construction, the one-dimensional van der Corput sequence, and its coordinatewise extension to a Halton sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b\ge 2\) be an integer. For \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), let \(k=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}a_j(k)b^j\) be its unique base-\(b\) digit expansion, with \(a_j(k)\in\{0,\ldots,b-1\}\) and only finitely many nonzero digits. Define \(\phi_b(k)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}a_j(k)b^{-j-1}\). The van der Corput sequence in base \(b\) is \((\phi_b(k))_{k\ge0}\). Given pairwise relatively prime integer bases \(p_1,\ldots,p_n\ge2\), the Halton sequence is \(\bigl((\phi_{p_1}(k),\ldots,\phi_{p_n}(k))\bigr)_{k\ge0}\subset[0,1)^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The radical inverse reflects the base-b digits of each nonnegative integer across the radix point. These values form the van der Corput sequence; applying the construction coordinatewise with pairwise relatively prime bases produces a Halton sequence in the unit cube.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k=\bigl(\phi_{p_1}(k),\ldots,\phi_{p_n}(k)\bigr)\in[0,1)^n\quad\text{for every }k\ge0

children.title: Randomized Covering Search
children.top_down_role: Randomized schemes designed to improve geometric coverage of the domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable probabilistic condition implying almost-sure candidate-pool density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(C_n\) consists of \(m_n\) iid draws from a full-support probability measure \(\mu\) on compact \(X\). For every rational \(\varepsilon>0\), choose a finite cover by \(K_\varepsilon\) balls of radius \(\varepsilon/2\), and let \(p_\varepsilon>0\) be the smallest \(\mu\)-mass of those balls. If \(\sum_nK_\varepsilon(1-p_\varepsilon)^{m_n}<\infty\) for every such \(\varepsilon\), then \(q_n\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-support candidate pools become dense almost surely when pool sizes make the probabilities of missing finite ball covers summable.
assumptions_latex: Draws within each pool are iid from a full-support measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_n\to0\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Smallest ball mass in the chosen cover

knowledge_statements.title: Random Candidate-Pool Density Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp support boundary for randomized covering search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every candidate pool is almost surely contained in a closed proper subset \(S\subsetneq X\), every selected site belongs to \(D_{n_0}\cup S\). If some \(x\in X\) has positive distance from that set, then \(\inf_n h(D_n)>0\). Maximin selection therefore cannot repair missing support in the candidate generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Farthest-candidate selection cannot cover regions that the candidate generator never proposes.
assumptions_latex: \(C_n\subset S\) almost surely for a closed proper subset \(S\subsetneq X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive distance from \(D_{n_0}\cup S\) forces fill distance to remain positive.

notation.meaning: Support subset of all candidate pools

knowledge_statements.title: Missing Candidate Support Prevents Coverage

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense Candidate Pools Yield Approximate Farthest-Point Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for maximin candidate selection to generate a dense evaluated design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, \(r_n(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,D_n)\), and choose \(x_{n+1}\in C_n\) satisfying \(r_n(x_{n+1})\ge\sup_{x\in C_n}r_n(x)-\eta_n\). If \(q_n=\sup_{x\in X}\operatorname{dist}(x,C_n)\to0\) and \(\eta_n\to0\), then the evaluated-design fill distance \(h(D_n)=\sup_{x\in X}r_n(x)\) tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate farthest-candidate selection becomes dense when candidate pools become dense and selection error vanishes.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Candidate Pools Yield Approximate Farthest-Point Coverage

assumptions_latex: The feasible region \(X\) is compact in a metric space \((X,\rho)\).
At iteration \(n\), a finite random candidate set \(C_n\subset X\) is generated.
Candidate sets become sufficiently dense so that their fill distance tends to zero almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f\) is continuous, the best evaluated value converges almost surely to \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Distance from a point to the current design
Random candidate set at iteration n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random candidate generation followed by a maximin coverage rule and incumbent selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial finite design \(D_{n_0}\subset X\). For \(n\ge n_0\), generate a finite random candidate set \(C_n\), select \(X_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C_n}r_n(x)\), evaluate \(f(X_{n+1})\), and set \(D_{n+1}=D_n\cup\{X_{n+1}\}\). Output a minimizer of \(f\) over \(D_n\). If the resulting fill distance \(h(D_n)=\sup_{x\in X}\min_{z\in D_n}\rho(x,z)\) tends to zero almost surely, then compactness and continuity imply that the incumbent objective value converges almost surely to the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate random candidates, evaluate the candidate farthest from prior sites, and retain the best point; vanishing fill distance yields global consistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Covering Search

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Randomized covering search with fixed-radius exclusion balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Samples from the currently uncovered region and removes a fixed-radius ball after each evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set $Z_1=A$ and $j=1$. At iteration $j$, sample $x_j$ from $P_{Z_j}$, evaluate $y_j=f(x_j)$, and compute $y_{oj}=\min_{1\leq i\leq j}y_i$. If the stopping condition is false, set $Z_{j+1}=Z_j\setminus B(x_j,\varepsilon,\rho)$, replace $j$ by $j+1$, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin with the full feasible region. Sample from the currently uncovered set, evaluate the objective, update the best observed value, and—unless stopping—remove the fixed-radius ball around the sample before continuing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_{oj}=\min_{1\leq i\leq j}f(x_i),\qquad Z_{j+1}=Z_j\setminus B(x_j,\varepsilon,\rho)\text{ when stopping does not occur}.
